...[as] suited for it as a doctor <note>In Böhme’s time, a "Doctor" specifically referred to a highly learned scholar or theologian.</note>, and even much better: for he exits his own reason and enters into God's mercy sooner; he does not possess great, wise reason, and therefore he does not take counsel with it, but goes simply with the poor tax-collector <note>A reference to the parable in Luke 18:9-14, where the humble tax-collector is justified before God rather than the prideful Pharisee.</note> into the Temple of Christ, whereas the highly learned man first puts a pair of spectacles <note>original: "Academiam auf die Nasen setzet"; literally "sets an academy on his nose." ### III. Of the Threefold Life, Chapter 7.

it [the soul] was also captured: For **Adam** was intended to be a lord over the stars and elements; nothing was to trouble him; he was all-powerful; he could have moved mountains with a single word; he was a master over fire, air, water, and earth, for there was no death in him. The light shone within him; he was in **Paradise**; paradisiacal fruit grew for him. He was *one human being*, and not two; he was the man and also the woman <note>Böhme refers here to the "Androgynous Adam," a common theme in his work where the original human contained both male and female spiritual principles before the Fall.</note>, and was meant to give birth to an angelic kingdom from within himself. And that was possible, for he did not have such flesh and blood as he did after the **Fall**, when he was ashamed of it before the Majesty of **God**. He had flesh and blood, but it was heavenly; his essences <term>essences: the fundamental spiritual qualities or "building blocks" of a being's nature</term> were holy. He could give birth without the tearing of his body, an image just like himself: for he was a virgin, without female form, after the form of the Eternal, with a pure, modest mind, and moreover chaste without desire. His desire was only for his own likeness out of himself; he contained his will within himself, and God was in him; thus his will was in God, and God in him, and he in Paradise. Yet he saw within himself at once two forms of the Divine Being: one outside of him in this world, and one within him in the Paradisiacal world, which he also possessed before him in full abundance.

26. Therefore the commandment came and spoke: *Do not eat of the mixed fruit, Evil and Good, otherwise you shall die.* (Genesis 2:17). But he imagined <note>original: "imaginirte"; in Böhme’s theology, "imagination" is the soul's power to focus its desire and "form" its own reality.</note> so long until he was captured: he always thought he wanted to eat of both and live eternally. He continued this for forty days, as long as the "other Adam" <note>Referring to Jesus Christ, the "Second Adam," during his forty days of temptation in the wilderness.</note> was tempted in the wilderness, and **Moses** was on the mountain where **Israel** was also tested, to see if it were possible to live in obedience and in the will of the Father. He carried this on until he sank down into sleep; for Moses says: *God let a deep sleep fall upon him* (Genesis 2:21), for when God saw that it was not possible for him—as desire had captured him—He let him fall asleep; this signifies death. Then the woman was made out of him; and the spirit of this world formed Adam into a man, as we still are; and **Eve** <note>original: "Hevam," the Latinized form of the name Eve.</note> into a woman, which they did not yet see when they awoke, for they were still in Paradise until they ate the earthly fruit. Then the spirit of this world took the soul captive, and in that hour their essences became earthly, and their flesh and blood became animalistic: of this they were ashamed, and became aware <note>That is, aware of their nakedness and their new, coarse physical forms.</note>

### Chapter 7. Of Humanity.

...of their animal form with their members of male and female form.

This light had previously lived and ruled within him; it now remained in its own Principle <term>Principle: Böhme’s term for one of the three fundamental realms of existence—the dark fire-world, the light-world, and the outer world of the senses.</term>, while the image remained in the outer Principle and was captured by the astral and elemental spirit. The governance of this world now resided in these humans, and they became earthly; then **God** also cursed the earth for man's sake, so that no more paradisiacal fruit grew. Everything was lost, except for **God’s** grace and mercy, which still remained. For they now stood with the foundation of the world in the abyss of hell among all the devils, and lived in frailty—just as we still do today—begetting children in two kingdoms. For the wrath of **God** had now captured them and wished to reveal its wonders in them. Likewise, the **Crusher of the Serpent** had also captured them into the light of life, and wished to reveal his wonders in them as well. There was strife and unrest, as can be seen in their children; the firstborn of the woman became a godless murderer and desired to suppress **God's** kingdom, and the second became a holy, pious man. In short <note>original: *In Summa*</note>, you see this throughout all Holy Scripture, especially with **Cain** and **Abel**, and with **Isaac** and **Ishmael**, as well as with **Esau** and **Jacob**, who struggled even in their mother's womb over the kingdom of **God** and the kingdom of hell.

28. Therefore **God** said: *Jacob I have loved, and Esau I have hated* (Romans 9:13). And from this originates the **Election of Grace** <term>Election of Grace: the theological concept that God chooses certain individuals for salvation by His mercy alone.</term> over the children who cling to Him. The others take what is said of **God** and the kingdom of heaven only as a mockery, and they do not find the noble **Philosopher’s Stone** <note>original: *Stein Philosophorum*; Böhme uses this alchemical term to represent the "Pearl of Great Price" or the indwelling spirit of Christ that transforms the "base metal" of the fallen human soul into spiritual "gold."</note>, for they do not seek it rightly; they are only hypocrites <term>Gleißner: a term for religious hypocrites who "glisten" with outward piety but lack inner truth.</term>, like the devil in the form of an angel; but **Abel**, **Isaac**, and **Jacob** found it well. **Jacob** wrestled a whole night for it, and **Isaac** carried his own firewood and was willing to let the darkness be burned away from his **Stone** voluntarily, for he had received the **Stone** in his mother's womb.

29. Look at King and Prophet **David**, how he acted with the **Stone** and how he loved it, for he said: *Even if my body and soul should break, you are nonetheless my—*

32. For we are enclosed with Adam in wrath, which holds us captive; yet grace also stands against us and desires us, and there is a great struggle within us. 34. This choice was not ordained by **God** in such a manner from eternity, for Adam was good and perfect, as well as pure, but he allowed himself to be overcome. For the **wrath** stood in the **abyss** <term>Abyss: In Böhme's thought, the *Ungrund* or the dark, chaotic potential that exists beneath the created world.</term>, and was hidden by the **Principle** of this world. And know this: that Adam's **Tree of Temptation** in Paradise—which nonetheless stood only in the abyss—grew out of the **Source of Wrath** <term>Source of Wrath: The 'dark fire' or harsh quality of nature that exists when not tempered by God's light and love.</term>. Had she turned her eyes away from the tree and the serpent, she would have remained in Paradise; after all, she had the Commandment. But because she followed the **Devil** and wished to be clever, she became a fool.

35. It is the same for us today: we are held captive by the abyss of **wrath**. The **Devil** presents us with the **glittering hypocrisy** <note>original: *Gleißnerey*. Refers to the deceptive, shining surface of worldly things.</note> of this world—its splendor, art, and riches— and we bite into it. Thus, we too are driven out of Paradise and lose the **Noble Stone**.

36. **Christ** instituted **Baptism** as a bath, so that we might wash away the **wrath**. He has bound the **Noble Stone** to us as a **godparent’s gift** <note>original: *Paten-Gelde*. A traditional gift of money given by godparents at a christening; here, Böhme uses it to describe the spiritual grace given in baptism.</note>, as the water of eternal life, so that we might step out of the **wrath** immediately in our childhood. But the serpent places itself before us, so that we fix our imagination upon the **Tree of Temptation**, as it stands before our eyes. When youth grows up a little, it crawls into splendor and hypocritical pride, and places the **Paradise-wreath** upon the serpent. Thus the serpent plays with them, teaching them all kinds of vanity, and leads them out of Paradise into this world, into splendor and pride. To this belongs **greed** and **falsehood**, so that one may satisfy such desires; thus the **Noble Stone** is then despised. Wherever one sees a person who carries the **Stone**, he must be their fool. The reason is this: they possess the **wit of the serpent**, and he who has the **Stone** is simple, without such wit, just like a child. His play in this world consists of sorrow, necessity, contempt, and misery; but it is written: *They go forth and weep, but they carry noble seed.* <note>A reference to Psalm 126:6.</note> Eternity is better than a brief moment of eye-pleasure followed by eternal mourning.

Bring fire! Oh run and flee, everyone, for the devil is there!" Thus they name the Spirit of **GOD**, because they do not know Him.

39. We do not write such things out of a desire to mock them, for we recognize the great misery of our own prison; rather, we do so because the simple person <note>original: *der Einfältige*. 41. Just as **God** the Father himself is all things; He is the <term>Trinity: original: *Drey-Zahl* (Three-Number). A term Böhme uses to describe the "quality" or "source" of a thing's nature, often implying a painful or agonizing tension that produces life.</term>; the fire is stinging, fierce, ravenous, and consuming; and the light is lovely, sweet, and longing, as if part of one body. Love desires the body, and the fire also desires the body for its food, but it consumes it entirely, whereas the light nourishes it and desires to fill it; it takes nothing from the body, but rather draws it up and makes it friendly.

42. Thus we consider ourselves, from whence a fierce and a good will arises; for you see in the fire that it has two spirits: one is the outflow of heat, and the other is the outflow of light. Now, the heat belongs to nature, and the light belongs to the eternal freedom outside of nature, for nature cannot grasp the light.

43. ...the higher it flies, the higher the light is, and they may well be called two <term>Principles: Böhme’s term for the fundamental realms: the dark fire-world and the light love-world.</term>; for the light desires <term>Essence: original: *Wesenheit*. ### Chapter 7. Of Man.
<header>Chapter 7. Of Man.</header>

Life burns; thus this <term>Fifth Essence: original: *Quinta Essentia*. In alchemy and early philosophy, the "quintessence" is the purest, most subtle element that permeates all nature beyond the four common elements.</term> is a cause of the burning of the stars.

46. The stars, however, contain all the causes of this world within them; everything that lives and moves is awakened by their property and brought to life. For they are not only fire and water (though fire and water are the most prominent things in them), but also hard, soft, dark, bitter, sour, and sweet; they possess all the powers of nature, everything that the earth itself contains. For every single star has a particular property, all according to the essences of the eternal <term>Center of Nature: original: *Centri Naturæ*. This refers to the inner core or generative pivot of natural existence.</term>. Everything in Creation was grasped and brought into being according to how many properties stood open at that same hour in the <term>Wheel of Nature: original: *Rade der Natur*. The dynamic, rotating force of existence that generates the various qualities of life.</term>, when Eternity moved itself toward Creation. And the air is the spirit, mixed with all forms. Just as heat goes out from fire, so the air always goes out from the fire and from all powers: therefore it is unstable. Soon one form in the Center of Nature awakens the spirit of air, and soon another; it is always in a state of wrestling and victory—now lying beneath, now rising above.

47. The entire depth between the earth and the stars is like the mind [Gemüth] of a human being. Just as the eyes might look at something, draw a will from it, and bring it into being—sometimes only with fleeting thoughts, and sometimes into a complete substance that the mouth and hands then take hold of—so the depth is also like a mind. Now it gazes fondly at one star, now at another. And the sun is the king and the heart of the depth; it shines and works within the depth, and so creates a life there. Just as the heart is in the body, so the sun is in the depth; and the other six planets constitute the senses and the understanding in the depth, so that all together it is like one living spirit. You can see this in the cattle, which draw their spirit from this environment, as well as in the birds, and also in us humans according to the <term>Adamic man: The physical, earthly aspect of humanity inherited from the first man, Adam, as opposed to the eternal spirit.</term>. But this governance and spirit does not have Divine understanding or wit, for it has a beginning and an end; and whatever has a beginning and an end is not spiritual or Divine, but natural and fragile. You see this in the wind: how quickly it is awakened in one place, and how quickly it settles again, only to rise in another, and so on.

48. Furthermore, the stars are a cause of all wisdom, art, and cunning; they are also a cause of all order and <term>governments: original: *Regimenten*. Refers to the systems of rule and social order among living beings.</term> in this world, among humans after the Fall, and also among the animals and birds. They are also a cause of, and awaken, all herbs and metals, and trees, so that they grow. For everything that the stars contain within themselves lies within the earth, and the stars set the earth on fire; all of this together is one spirit, one government, which I call the <term>Third Principle: original: *Principium*. In Boehme's cosmology, the first principle is the dark fire/wrath, the second is the light/love, and the third is the visible, material world.</term>. For it is the third life in God, the awakened life, and not an eternal one. In this life, only the great wonders that lie in the <term>Center of eternal nature: original: *Centro*. The inner generative source of all things.</term> are meant to be brought into visible being. The form of these wonders remains eternally, but not in their essences—those all return again into the <term>Ether: original: *Æther*. The subtle, atmospheric substance from which the material elements arose.</term>. Just as it was before the Creation, so it shall be again at the end. However, everything from this world remains standing in Eternal Nature with its colors and shapes, like a painted being; otherwise, the creatures—such as angels and humans, who are eternal—would have no joy.

49. Thus, they will be powerful over all things, and there will still be a greening, blooming, and growing, but without the knowledge of <term>grimness: original: *Grimmes*. The harsh, wrathful, or bitter quality found in the dark foundation of nature.</term> and fire. For the essences are no longer a material being, and therefore there is no fire; that fire is an eternal darkness, a gnawing within itself, and that is called eternal death, of which the Scripture testifies in all places. Do not consider this a trivial thing, for it is true; we speak faithfully of what we recognize in our <note>The "Mother's womb" here refers to the source of Divine Wisdom or the inner spirit of Nature where the author receives his insights.</note> Mother’s womb.

## Chapter 8.

->That besides this earthly life, another life exists within us.<-

->Summaries.<-

The inner fire is gentle and burns in desire; its spirit is love and joy, and its essence is heavenly earth, §. 1. and this angelic world is called the <term>Holy Ternary: original: *Ternarius Sanctus*. A Latin term for the Holy Trinity, here referring to the divine manifestation in the spiritual world.</term>. 2. Thus every angel and human is like God: ibid. He has the <term>Trinity: original: *Drey-zahl*. The threefold nature of God.</term> within himself, and the Holy Spirit also goes out within him. 3. The author writes this from God’s <term>revelation: original: *Offenbarung*.</term> 4. Adam was in Paradise in the body of God, and went out into the government of this world. 5. Here, nothing helps but the <term>new birth: original: *neue Geburt*. The spiritual rebirth required to reconnect with the divine life.</term>; the Divine fire must be ignited, then the devil cannot attack, but must flee from the person.

This life contains all the qualities of this world within it, but not in such ignited essences, for it has no fire <note>In Böhme’s thought, "fire" often refers to the harsh, consuming, or wrathful aspect of nature. The eternal world has heat and light, but not the destructive "fire" of the material realm.</note>: although it does have a mighty fire, it burns in a different quality <note>original: *Qual*. Referring to the "Ungrund," the bottomless or groundless mystery of God's primal state.</note>: it has its own growth and blooming, though not from such earth as ours—and yet it *is* earth, which in my whole book I call Substantiality <note>original: *Wesenheit*. There is no need, misery, or wretchedness within it, and one knows nothing of such things; neither is death, the devil, or wrath known there; rather, all those things remain hidden in darkness in the first <term>Principle: original: *Principio*. The first of Böhme's three principles, representing the dark, fiery source or potentiality of God.</term>.

A Latin term referring to the divine trinity as expressed in a "holy body" or a perfected state of being.</term>, and quite rightly so: Although the Latin language understands by this only the "number three," the Language of Nature <note>original: *Natur-Sprache*. A central Böhme concept meaning the inner, universal language where the names of things reveal their true essences.</note> grasps it all together as one body; for just as this principle of our world is all together but one body; so too are God, the Kingdom of Heaven, angels, man, and Paradise, with all heavenly and divine beings and qualities—all are but one body, which together is called God, Majesty, and Eternity. For Majesty is the light of that body, and the Holy Spirit is its delight and spirit of life; but the creatures have their own life-spirit from within themselves: for every angel and human is like the whole of God.

3. 9. For there is no other will in **GOD** but to save that which is lost; therefore, no man should despair. For if the soul-spirit <term>soul-spirit: *Seelen-Geist*, the higher, active part of the human soul that can direct itself toward the divine</term> truly raises itself up, it is stronger than **GOD**, and overcomes **GOD**; for the Wrath <note>In Böhme’s theology, God’s "Wrath" is the harsh, fiery foundation of existence that must be overcome by His "Love."</note> is also **GOD'S**, and is **GOD'S** greatest power, yet the soul overcomes it; it is stronger than the abyss of Hell; it can move mountains without a storm, only by its will.

10. For through the Will, **GOD** created Heaven and Earth. And such a mighty will is also hidden within the soul, yet it now swims there in misery, in great weakness, bound within the sinking of death, and allows itself to be led like a poor captive creature from one mire into another. Now the Devil leads it into one puddle, then into another, and it looks like a stained cloth, full of impurity: all the stars pour their poison into the body and defile the poor soul; it must allow itself to be defiled by all the animals, for the body eats the flesh of animals, and with this the poor soul is clothed.

11. Do you know why **GOD** forbade the Jews certain meats? Light their fat and observe its property, then you will see it. <note>Böhme suggests that the spiritual "quality" or essence of certain foods directly affects the spiritual fire of the soul.</note> The poor soul is a fire that burns there; now, when such a property enters the soul’s fire, do you think **GOD** will dwell within? Therefore **Christ** teaches us and says: "Be sober and temperate in eating and drinking; watch and pray, for your adversary the devil walks about like a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour." 1 Peter 5:8.

12. Thus you see how we stand in a threefold life: The soul stands upon the abyss between two principles <term>two principles: the "Dark World" of fire/wrath and the "Light World" of love/grace</term> and is bound to both, and the body is merely in this world, living from the spirit of this world; therefore it seeks only food and drink, power and honor, for it belongs to the earth and cares little for the poor soul, which is from eternity. So we must now tame the body, give it no room, dampen its desires, and not fill it whenever it wishes, but only for necessity, so that it does not become a lecherous donkey and invite the devil in as a guest.

For it has its own spirit, so that it lives and grows, and then consumes itself again, doing so time after time: for such a being is the bond of eternity, which is called Nature.

16. Thus we humans have an even higher knowledge and understanding, for we can look into the heart of all things to see what their essence and quality may be. We also have a different longing and desire for another essence and life, which is not animalistic and transitory, and which does not desire elemental, earthly food.

17. So we recognize now that every life desires its mother, from whom it originates and in whom it stands. It is recognizable to us that every life desires the best that is in its Center <note>original: *Centro*; Böhme uses this to describe the focal point of divine or natural forces.</note>, such as the Heart or Oil <note>original: *Oleum*</note>, in which the fire burns and the life stands open, so that it is a life.

18. For every life is like a fire, and yet the torment of the fire is not the true life, but rather the Tincture <term>Tincture: In Böhme’s theosophy, the spiritual quintessence or animating power that transforms the "fire" of existence into "light" and joy.</term> which originates from the fire. That is a lovely delight and is the Freedom of Nature; for Nature stands in great anguish <note>The German *Angst* here implies a narrowing, pressure, or constriction—the labor pains of existence.</note> and forces itself so hard with desire for freedom until it reaches it. And when it reaches it, Nature becomes a sharpness within that freedom and wants to consume the freedom into itself so that it might entirely become one with it. Yet it cannot; the more it rages and rises up toward freedom, the greater the Tincture of freedom becomes. Thus Nature remains a fire, and freedom remains a light. What the Tincture builds, the fire eats; for the Tincture creates essence <note>original: *Wesenheit*</note>, and its center is gentle and is a sinking down, just as the fire is a rising up.

19. But because the light, acting as the Tincture, creates essence in its sinking—so that an essence like water is in the light, and yet not water, but such a spirit and quality—the fire consumes that same essence into itself. Through this, its wrath <note>original: *Grimm*; often referring to the harsh, consuming quality of base nature or divine judgment.</note> is extinguished, and it rises up in the essence and burns just like a fire in oil. This is the true natural life of all creatures, and it is called Tincture.

20. Now, however, this life is fragile, for it has a beginning and stands only in four forms: in fire, air, water, and in the essence which is the body. Thus it is a pulling-in and a fleeing-away: for the fire wants to have the fleeing essence back by force, and this is a perpetual struggle.

21. Thus you see this, and it is quite clear, how the fire of life lets the air out from itself, for the air also does not want to remain in the fire's torment, but flees with power; and the fire's torment pulls the air back into itself again and again. Thus the fire is blown up <note>i.e., stoked or inflated like a bellows</note>, otherwise it would suffocate and become dark. For these reasons, it reaches for the essence as air, for no torment desires the enclosure of death—and it is called death when life is enclosed. Furthermore, there is no death, for in eternity there has never been any death, nor will there ever be; rather, that which is called "eternal death" is an enclosure of the <term>Tincture: The spiritual life-force or "dye" that transforms the raw fire of nature into light and beauty.</term>. When the <term>Tincture</term> retreats like a figure, the Center <note>original: *Centrum*; the focal point of natural forces.</note> remains as the fire-source in the darkness, and it wells up in pure fierceness <note>original: *Grimmigkeit*; a state of wrath or harsh, dark energy.</note> within itself. It would dearly love to reach the <term>Tincture</term> again, yet it has no power to do so, for the <term>Tincture</term> alone is the power which blows up the fire.

22. Here, reflect upon hell and eternal death, for that is what it is; and understand that the devils have lost the <term>Tincture</term> of gentleness <note>original: *Sanfftmuth*; the cooling, loving aspect of the divine light.</note>, and are now a fierce fire-source without essence, for they have no body. And then, secondly, reflect upon the element of water: just as you recognize that it originates in the spirit of the creature, so it also does in the depths of the world, which is also a spirit and has a life just like a creature. And then thirdly, reflect on how there are two kinds of fire: a hot one and a cold one. # Chapter 9. Of Man.

Grasping: <note>original: "Griff"; completing a thought from the previous page regarding a prideful or ambitious "grip" on life.</note> so too is he minded, and he satisfies this inclination as much as he can. And then, secondly, he desires wealth, goods, and money, much eating and drinking; he does not care how he obtains these things. This is the **spirit of this world**, which desires only abundance and luxury, just as an animal does.

18. And then thirdly, he also desires the **kingdom of heaven**; he sighs and wishes for it, but in great weakness. He stands always in doubt, thinking he is a sinner and that God does not want him. Nevertheless, he sighs longingly for it and would gladly be saved; he prays, and yet he also doubts; he hopes and wavers. He hopes for restraint <note>original: "Abstinenz"; in Böhme’s context, this refers to a spiritual renunciation or turning away from worldly impulses.</note> and redemption from one day to the next. He always thinks, "Tomorrow it will be better; tomorrow you will have the strength to go out into another life." This is how he carries on continually.

19. We are not speaking here of the **swine-men** <note>original: "Säu-Menschen"; Böhme's term for people who live entirely animalistic lives in the "muck" of physical desires.</note>, who lie only in the filth and never once seek restraint; rather, we speak of the poor sinner caught between heaven and hell, who feels the impulse of both and yet allows himself to be held back.

20. Now see, what does man do? He follows all three impulses. He always seeks power and honor until his end; he always seeks greed, money, and goods, eating and drinking. And even if he has more than enough, he still does not have enough in his greed; he acts as if he should live here forever. And then thirdly, he does indeed sigh: for the poor soul is very anxious, and fears forever the devil and God’s wrath, and would gladly be redeemed. But the first two kingdoms <note>The "kingdoms" of worldly pride and animal desire.</note> press the soul down and lock it in their dungeon, so that many a poor soul even becomes despondent, plunges into the abyss, and despairs of God’s kingdom.

21. It is said: the **devil** comes to man in the **form of an angel**; and that is true. See what he does so that he may be held as an angel and pious: when the poor soul shows itself to be restless, and frequently sets death and God’s wrath before the eyes of the body, the devil does not resist it. He often lets the poor soul run away with the body into heaps of stones, or wherever it wishes to go. Most of all, he leads it into the **masonry-churches** <note>original: "Mauer-Kirchen"; Böhme uses this term to distinguish the physical building made of stone from the "temple" of the human heart where true worship happens.</note>, and then speaks to the soul: "You are indeed pious, for you like to go to church."

...speaks of the **new birth**, he sows other thoughts in the **spirit of this world** within man; perhaps his own spirit, perhaps he turns his eyes toward pride and physical beauty; perhaps he captures the spirit with the pleasure of **imagination** <note>Böhme uses "imagination" to describe the soul's power to "image" or shape itself into what it desires.</note> toward men or women, depending on one's sex, and tickles the heart with passion <note>original: "Brunst"; referring to an intense, disordered heat or lust.</note>, or even with sleep.

Better to have slept than to have imagined in passion or to have embraced slander.

25. Oh, you **sophists**, who spend your sermons slandering the ancients who have long been dead, who out of envy and desire often slander pious hearts: how will you stand with your little sheep, whom you should lead to graze on green meadows and guide onto Christ’s paths toward **love, chastity, and humility**, and yet you pour slander into them? You would be better off with your unjust slander in a cattle stall than in the **pulpit** <note>original: "Canzel".</note>, for there you would lead no one astray.

26. ### Chapter 9. Of Man.

27. The other devil is more cunning <note>original: "künstlicher"; implying both artistic craftsmanship and deceptive skill.</note> than this one; he also appears as a shining angel, yet with **cow's feet**. Then the heart stands there and counts out the words of the prayer one after another, as it has perhaps learned them, and the devil takes the power from the heart so that the soul cannot seize the <term>Center of Nature</term> <note>original: "Centrum Naturæ"; Böhme's term for the inner spiritual core where the divine fire is ignited.</note> with a **siege-storm** <note>original: "Mauersturm"; a military metaphor for intense, forceful prayer that "storms the gates" of heaven or the heart.</note>, as Christ says: *The devil takes the word from their hearts, so that they might not believe and be saved.* Luke 8:12.

He is always merciful, and there is no other will in Him but to be merciful. He can do nothing else; His arms are spread out day and night toward the poor sinner. And if one comes and thus storms hell, there is greater joy before **God’s** angels than for ninety-nine righteous ones who do not need it, as **Christ** Himself teaches us. Luke 15:7.

# III. Of the Threefold Life Chapter 9.

...disputed with him <note>the devil</note> because of the multitude of sins, but rather gathered all sin into one heap—even if they were as many as the sand by the sea—and threw them onto the devil’s neck, saying in the heart: "Look here, devil, you are the cause of all this evil; I offer the sin to you, but **God’s** mercy and the death of Christ to me; in this I will involve myself. If you can, then devour me." And thus, one should set oneself firmly upon Christ’s promise and place the entire storm within Christ’s death, wounds, and suffering, and into His love. Do not dispute much further with sin, for the devil only entangles himself in it and forces sin upon you so that you should despair.

31. Try it then, and you will soon see and feel another person, with another mind and will. We speak as we know and have experienced ourselves, and not in imaginings or opinions, or from history books, but from that which we have a foundation; for a soldier knows what it is like in war, but he who has not experienced it and was never there always thinks otherwise. We report such things for teaching and instruction out of love, as a spirit (of Christ) who speaks of how it happened to him, as an example to others; if anyone wishes to follow us, he will experience whether it be true.

### The Gate of the Deep Ground of Man.

32. From the beginning of the world, there has been a quarrel over this, because this gate was sunken away with Adam, and we have been held captive in darkness. But because **God** grants it to us and opens it, and also gives a strong will for the writing down of it, we shall do so; and thank **God** the Father in Christ **Jesus** in eternity, who has redeemed us from the darkness of death.

33. *   **The Sun** ($\odot$): Located near the center, representing the second principle of Light and the "Heart of God."

*   **Heavenly Majesty** <note>original: "Himliſche Majeſtät"</note>: The second principle, the Kingdom of Light and Love.
*   **THREE** <note>original: "DREY"</note>: Referring to the **Three Principles** <term>Böhme’s system of the Dark World, Light World, and the Outspoken (Visible) World</term> or the Trinity.

And on the third day He tested the work, and let forms and images arise out of the earth from the essences, such as trees, herbs, and grass: these were images of the essences of desire. But the Spirit’s image still remained hidden, and yet was in the essence, until the fourth day; here, understand a "day" without a sun is a revolution of the wheel of <term>Nature</term> <note>original: *Naturæ* (Latin). Böhme envisions nature as a cyclical, seven-fold wheel of spiritual "spirits" or qualities</note> in the desire of the will. ### III. Of the Threefold Life Chap. 10.

The stubborn man remains rigid in his own will and does not want to surrender it to **GOD**; he trusts in his own cleverness. Thus his will is outside of **GOD** and can do nothing: And so, when he speaks from himself about **GOD**'s essence and will, he is an ignorant liar, for he does not speak from **GOD**'s Spirit and will, but from himself, out of his own delusion, in which there is nothing but doubt. From this arise the disputes of faith concerning Divine Science <note>original: "Göttliche Wissenschaft"; in Böhme’s time, this referred to the systematic knowledge of God or theology</note>, because people seek **GOD** in their own human will and knowledge. People want to find **GOD** in their own will, and He is not in there; for He dwells only and solely in the will that surrenders itself entirely to Him with all reason and knowledge. To such a person, He gives the recognition and power to know His essence.

51. Therefore lift up your heads and take note: God's will is found in no quarrel or strife, but rather in the will of humans and the devil; it is the will of the wrath of **GOD**. Do not let yourselves be led astray by the hypocrites who parade about in historical knowledge <note>original: "in der Historien"; referring to those who only know the Bible as a dead history rather than a living spirit</note> and say: "We have **GOD**'s will with us, we are His servants, look at us, we are **GOD**'s officials; and even if we are evil, we still carry out the office and will correctly." O cursed nature of Cain and Judas, you are not born or known in **GOD**—how then can you boast of **GOD**'s will? How can you say you carry the *Great Mystery* <note>original: "Mysterium Magnum"; the hidden, foundational secret of God's manifestation</note> of **GOD**, when you are outside of **GOD** in a foreign will and in your own self? You do not carry the *Great Mystery*; rather, it is the poor sinner who turns back, who has been captured by the devil and is in a struggle against the devil, who groans, sighs, and cries out to **GOD**. Such a person runs in repentance and abstinence to the office of the *Great Mystery*, which *Christ* gave to His disciples and children who are within the will of **GOD**; they truly possess the key to Heaven and Hell. Now, you *Sophist* <note>A term Böhme uses for academic theologians who prioritize logic and dogma over spiritual experience</note> do not carry the office because you are outside of **GOD**'s will. Instead, the poor, penitent person brings the *Great Mystery* with him to you, and surrenders himself to the Apostolic power—which you do not possess, but which belongs to the Community of *Christ* <note>original: "Gemeine Christi"</note> who are within **GOD**'s will. Thus, one faith receives the other, and the Community of *Christ* *absolves* <note>original: "absolviret"; provides spiritual forgiveness or release from sin</note> the penitent sinner, and not you, *Sophist*, you who have neither power, might, nor knowledge of the Kingdom of **GOD**, but are yourself a prisoner.

And the inner delight of the eternal Center presses out with the Spirit of God into the **Heart of the Sun** <note>original: "Hertze Solis"</note>, which is the great life and fire that melts stones and earth, within which the eternal **Tincture** <note>original: "Tinctur"; a spiritual essence or "dye" that transforms and ennobles matter.</note> is recognized in the ninth number.

20. Thus, understand also the "breathing in": The external government of the spirit of this world, which reaches as far as the sun, was breathed into him from the outside as an external life. And the internal government from the inner fire in the eighth number <note>The "eighth number" in Böhme's system represents the transition from the harshness of nature to the light of the spirit.</note> was breathed into his heart from the inside out. For that same life was from the eternal fire, which reaches toward the Cross into the ninth number according to its own Tincture, which goes toward the **Trinity** <note>original: "Dreyzahl"</note> as if into eternal freedom. There, man became a living soul, with spirit and soul; for the soul originates one degree deeper than the sun, from the eternal fire that burns in the eternal will—which will is to give birth to the Heart of God and to elevate the brilliance of the Majesty into the wonders.

21. Therefore, understand us correctly: The Holy Spirit of God awakened the living soul from the Center of eternal nature upon the Cross, as its own Center—not out of the Trinity, but out of eternal nature, out of the fire of the Center of Nature in the fifth form of the Center. Where the two kingdoms divide—namely, God’s love and wrath—there the Spirit of God awakened the soul and led it from the inside out into the Tincture of the external spirit, into the heart's blood, through Himself; that is the soul.

22. My Lord Doctor, understand this rightly, and do not walk about so pridefully, for the soul is God's child. Its will should be constantly placed in God's will, in the tenth number <note>The "tenth number" represents the highest state of perfection and the throne of God.</note>; then it is an angel, and lives in God, and eats of God’s word, of God's power and life. It should not turn back into the spirit of this world, into the fire of the **out-birth** <note>original: "Ausgeburt"; Böhme's term for the physical, manifested world that was "born out" of the spiritual realm.</note>, but into the fire of the Trinity, into the **Holy Sanctuary** <note>original: "Ternarium Sanctum"; referring to the holy realm of the Triune God.</note>.

### III. Of the Threefold Life Chapter 11.

23. Now you understand what you are, and what you were before the Fall; for you could rule over the sun and stars. Everything that lived feared you. You had your own food from the paradisical fruit to give to the external life, and for the internal soul-life, you had the **Word of the Lord** <term>Verbum Domini; the creative speech of God that sustains the spirit.</term>. You would have lived eternally without woe or the feeling of any kind of sickness in pure joy and delight, and moreover, without effort or sorrow. Your mind would have been like that of a child playing with the wonders of its father. No knowledge of an evil will would have been within you; no greed, no pride, no envy, no anger, but all would have been a game of love.

24. Now see that you grasp this: God undertook a special day's work with man. Had He intended for him to be earthly, animal-like, and mortal, He would surely have created him on the fifth day with the other animals. He loved himself, and through himself, God. For he had a body that could pass through trees and stones, provided he had remained within the will of God; for that will would have led him along with itself into the great wonders.

### III. Of the Threefold Life, Chapter 11.

61. See, you poor wounded soul, you stand and pray: "O God, forgive me my sin, let your wrath subside, and receive me into grace!" This is quite right; however, you do not understand how God receives the poor sinner. You imagine it is just as when you come before your earthly sovereign <note>original: "Lands-Fürsten"; a territorial prince or local ruler.</note> after having forfeited your life, and you plead with him, and he forgives your misdeed out of grace, and so you are acquitted. But your sins still scold you to your face, and your own heart accuses you that you are still deserving of punishment. See, this is also how you come before God, and through this, many hypocrites are born. You think God, in His Being and Spirit, takes your sin away from you. Do you not know what the Scripture says: *that all our works shall follow us*? If it happened that way, then God would have to move Himself for the sake of every person who calls upon Him and cast their sin away from them. Yet God has not moved Himself more than twice from eternity: once with the creation of the world and all creatures, and then secondly in the **Incarnation of Christ** <note>original: "Menschwerdung Christi"; the act of God becoming human.</note>; that is when the Heart of God moved.

62. See, when God forgives your sin when you call upon Him, He takes nothing away from you, nor does He descend from heaven into you, for He has been in your soul from eternity—but in His **Principle** <term>Principle: Böhme uses the Latin term "Principio" to refer to the foundational source or the specific "realm" of existence (either the dark fire-world or the light-world).</term>. Your soul merely went out from Him, from His Principle—understand: from the holy will of the Majesty—into the **Wrath** <note>original: "Zorn"; in Böhme’s cosmology, the "Wrath" is the dark, consuming fire of God's power that becomes "hell" when separated from His light.</note>. Now you were in the Wrath in eternal death, and the man Christ, who is God and man, has made a path through death and wrath to the **Majesty** <note>original: "Majestät"; the radiant, light-filled glory of God's presence.</note> of God. You must only turn around and go through that same path—through the death of Christ, through the wrath—into the Majesty; then you will be received like the dearest angel who never had any sin. Nor will any sin be recognized in you, but only God’s **wonder-deed** <note>original: "Wunderthat"; a miraculous act of divine manifestation.</note>, which had to be revealed in the wrath; for Love could not achieve that in the fire—she does not mix herself into the fire, but rather flees from it.

63. Now, when you pray thus: "O God, forgive me!" you are also still constantly doubting because of your sin, wondering whether God will hear you and come into your heart. See, do not do that, for with your doubt you show contempt for the Majesty...

Afterward, you will surely have release and relief in your heart; you will receive a Guide <note>Referring to the Holy Spirit or the inner presence of Christ.</note> who draws you, and who sets the falsehood of the world before your eyes and warns you against it.

<meta>This page continues the critique of externalized religion and the false assurance of forgiveness. ### Chapter 11. Of Man.

[The institutional church] claims to hold the key to indulgences <note>German: Ablass. The practice of granting the remission of temporal punishment for sins, which Böhme famously critiqued as being corrupted by financial motives.</note>, asserting that it can forgive sins. It boasts of the **Apostolic Key** <note>A reference to the "Keys of the Kingdom of Heaven" given to St. Peter (Matthew 16:19), which the Papacy claimed as the basis for its authority.</note>, and sells the forgiveness of sins for money, deriving this from Christ’s words: *Whosesoever sins ye remit, they are remitted unto them* (John 20:23).

69. Now, I would dearly like to know how the sins of a repentant sinner—who throws himself into God’s will and departs from the "reason" of this world into God’s mercy—could possibly be "retained" <note>Referring to the second half of John 20:23: "...and whosesoever sins ye retain, they are retained." Böhme argues that if a person truly turns to God, no priest has the power to "retain" or keep those sins on the soul.</note>. Even more, I would like to know how one sinful person can lead another out of hell and into the Kingdom of Heaven when he himself cannot enter it, but sits there merely to flatter the devil for the sake of his own spirit, all while selling the forgiveness of sins for money. For all sins are drowned in the new body of Christ, in Christ’s flesh and blood; and Isaiah, speaking in the person of Christ, says: *I have trodden the winepress alone... and of the people there was none with me* (Isaiah 63:3). If it were true, as the Antichrist <note>Böhme frequently used "Antichrist" to refer to the corrupt institutional church structures of his day.</note> boasts, then one devil would have to drive out another. And if that were to happen, what would become of the **rebirth** through Christ’s flesh and blood, by which our souls are led into God? If it had been possible for God to take away Adam’s sin in such a [superficial] way, God would not have become human to lead us back into Himself. He would have simply forgiven Adam his sin, just as a prince grants a murderer his life. No, friend <note>Original German: "Fritz," used here as a colloquial or generic address to the reader, similar to "my dear fellow."</note>, you must depart from sin yourself and enter into God’s will. For God does not stand there like a [human] king, forgiving sin merely with words: there must be **power**; you must go out of the fire and into the light. For God is not a mere image before whom we step and offer fine words; rather, He is a Spirit, and He penetrates the heart and the kidneys—that is, the soul and the spirit. He is the **Fire of Love**, and the <term>Centrum Naturae</term> <note>The "Center of Nature." In Böhme's philosophy, this is the fundamental "kitchen" or core of existence where the dark, longing desires of nature are either transformed into light or remain in "wrathful fire."</note> is His **Fire of Wrath**. You are in God, even if you are with all the devils in hell; for the Wrath is also His—it is His abyss. When you enter into sin, you enter into the abyss; but when you go out of it, you enter into God’s love, into the freedom from all torment.

70. There is no other forgiveness available than this: that you depart from the will of this world, the flesh, and the devil, and enter into God’s will. Then God’s will receives you, and you are free of all sins, for they remain behind in the fire,

### Chapter 11. Of the Human Being.

79. No human being has any power in God, unless he is in God’s will, in God’s love in Christ, and possesses Christ’s soul and flesh. If he possesses these, then he is no greedy man or hypocrite who sells the kingdom of heaven for money. When Simon Magus offered Saint Peter money so that he might give him the power to bestow the Holy Spirit on whomever he laid his hands, Peter said: "May you be cursed with your money; do you think the gifts of God are sold for money?" <note>Referring to Acts 8:18–24, where the term "simony"—the buying or selling of ecclesiastical privileges—originates.</note> Where then, you <term>Sophists</term> <note>Böhme uses "Sophists" as a derogatory term for academic theologians and clergy who rely on logic, book-learning, and institutional status rather than direct spiritual experience.</note>, do you get such power that you sell the kingdom of heaven and pull it into your own authority? You are not Christ’s disciples, but the disciples of the Antichrist, of the <note>original: "Huren zu Babel"</note> Whore of Babylon. No priest is fit for his office unless he is in God's will; his <term>absolution</term> <note>The formal act of a priest pronouncing forgiveness of sins.</note> is no absolution at all. Instead, the community of Christ, to which he submits himself, absolves him; he is as useful to the church as a fifth wheel is to a wagon. You Sophist, how can you communicate the <term>Great Mystery</term> <note>original: "Mysterium Magnum." In Böhme’s thought, this is the "Chaos" or the hidden, unmanifested source of all things from which the world and the spirit proceed.</note> which you do not possess? The community possesses it, and the repentant sinner who comes to you possesses it, but you are merely a Sophist. You would be better off in a cowshed than in a church; how can the devil absolve a repentant person? You serve only your idol, the belly.

80. O you blind world, how blinded you are! You imagine that you must not touch the Great Mystery, that you are not capable of it, and that the priest alone is capable. If you are in Christ, then you have everything freely; you have His covenant with Baptism and the Sacrament, and the body and blood of Christ within them. For the covenant belongs to the believers, and not to the Sophists. Indeed, Christ’s disciples, and their disciples after them, and those who followed, baptized; and the believing community broke Christ’s bread in houses and wherever they could, and enjoyed the body and blood of Christ. The temple of God was everywhere that Christians were together.

81. We do not report such things in order to tear down the churches in which one carries out Christ’s office; rather, we are showing you the hypocrites who bind you to themselves, so that you may go out from them to the community of Christ. Enter into the temple of Christ, and do not let yourselves be satisfied merely with the <term>wall-church</term> <note>German: "Mauer-Kirchen." So if you now see that the world wrangles over Christ's cup <note>A reference to the fierce theological disputes between Lutherans, Calvinists, and Catholics regarding the nature of the Eucharist or Lord's Supper.</note>, then know that they have lost the key of the **Great Mystery** <note>original: "Mysterium Magnum." In Böhme’s thought, this is the "Chaos" or the hidden foundation of all existence from which the spiritual and material worlds emerge.</note> and are not in Christ; for in Christ there is no wrangling, but only love and humility, and the desire for one’s neighbor’s righteousness.

90. Where we are, there we are in Christ: When we come together, we should all bring one single Will into the community, namely the desire for Christ. And if we desire Him, then we receive Him, and are one body in Him. He feeds us with his body and gives us his blood to drink: When we observe the custom of his Testament with the Last Supper, there He feeds us with his flesh and gives us his blood to drink; He baptizes us with the baptism into one body in Him. Why do we seek or search for so long? Just as the sun's radiance fills the whole world, so also do Christ's body and blood: His essence is eternity, where there is no place or location; He is enclosed in nothing, for He is in the Father, and the Father is in Him, and the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father and the Son. Now all beings are created out of the Father, and the Father is in all and sustains all: He gives life and being to everything, and the Son is in the Father and gives everything power and light; He is our light, and without Him we do not recognize **God**. How then do we wish to speak rightly of Him? If we wish to speak rightly of Him, then we must speak from His Spirit, for that Spirit bears witness of **God**; but if we speak from human art and history <note>As noted on the previous page, Böhme uses "history" (Historie) to mean academic, intellectual knowledge that lacks personal spiritual experience.</note>, then we speak from ourselves and not from **God**, and are murderers and thieves, and not Christ’s shepherds. A thief comes only to steal and rob; thus the wranglers also come in their own name, only because they wish to have a great reputation and want to have rich prebends <note><term>prebends</term>: Lucrative church offices or stipends often granted to clergy regardless of their spiritual merit.</note>. They cry out: "Christ is here!" (claiming that Christ is presented to the community only by us through his Word), "there are the heretics!"

91. Dear children of Christ, stop your ears against these vicious wolves; for they do not only shame themselves among one another, but also the community of Christ, which is everywhere in all lands. Wherever there are repentant people who regret their sins and turn away from them, and place themselves into the mercy...

He who wants to slay the Antichrist is the Antichrist’s beast upon which he rides; he only becomes more powerful through wrangling; for the hearts are turned away from the truth and go out...

### Chapter 11. Of Man.

<note>original: "Zanck," referring to the bitter theological disputes between Lutheran, Calvinist, and Catholic factions during the 17th century.</note> When God is caught in wrangling, everyone loses themselves in the wonders of the dispute and chases after magnificent speeches; thus they depart from Christ and fall into "opinions" <note>To Böhme, "opinions" are man-made dogmas that distract from the direct experience of God's light.</note>, seeking paths in darkness where there is no light. 95. This is also what happened to the mighty lands where the Quran <note>original: "Alcoran."</note> rules. But the Antichristian kingdom (the yoke) lives in many trees; they run from one to another and do not know which is the best, for they have departed from the Paradise of Christ. They only want to keep a sign of Him, so that they can occupy Christ’s place in their own pride <note>original: "Hoffart," implying a haughty, worldly arrogance.</note> and thus remain fine, rich, fat bellies. They say, "He is in heaven; we will establish a glittering and magnificent kingdom in His honor, so that through His office we may attain good times and honor. If someone has died, even if he was an unjust, false usurer <note>Someone who lends money at high interest; Böhme frequently critiques the emerging capitalist ethics of his time.</note>, a whoremonger, a murderer, or a thief all his life—and even if they know this—if he (or his family) only gives enough money, oh, how magnificently and blessedly they praise him! What great memorial-notes <note>original: "Denck-Zettel," likely referring to funeral orations or written testimonials of character purchased from the church.</note> they produce, so that another unjust man might hear it, follow the same path, and then—

# III. Of the Threefold Life, Chapter 11.

[Wis]dom played with us: but when He created us in the wits <note>original: "Witze," referring here to our consciousness and creative understanding</note>, we were meant to play with and among one another; but the Devil begrudged us this and made us disagree in our play, which is why we still quarrel. We have nothing else to quarrel about except in our play: when that is over, we lay ourselves down to rest and go home; then others come to play and quarrel until evening, until they go to sleep in their own land, from which they came: For we were in the land of peace, but the Devil talked us into going into his unpeaceful land.

108. Dear children, what are we doing, that we obey the Devil? # Chapter 12.

->Concerning the Christian Life and Conduct: What man is to do in this valley of tears <term>valley of tears: a common biblical metaphor (Psalm 84:6) for the suffering and transience of earthly life</term>, so that he may perform God’s work, and thus attain the eternal highest good.<-

### Summary Points.

1. Man should learn to know himself. §. 1. 
2. His soul-will is eternal; whatever he grasps <note>meaning whatever the soul focuses its desire upon</note>, he takes with him. 2. 
3. Therefore, it is good to choose the best. 3. 
4. In heaven, mostly the poor will appear, 4. 5. 
5. and nothing but love will be within it. 6. 
6. Therefore, in this time, we should enclose ourselves in humility and love, and be one in Christ. 7.

8. A virginal song of praise. 10.

13. All war and strife have arisen from the Antichrist. 15.

Nothing is more necessary and useful to man in this valley of tears on earth than that he learns to know himself: what he is, where he is from, or where he wishes to go? What he strives for, and where he travels when he dies? To know this is most useful for everyone. For our outward conduct remains in this world; but what the heart grasps, the person takes with them.

2. The will of the soul-spirit is eternal: whatever is enclosed within the soul-spirit’s will, that the soul takes with it when body and soul part from one another. <note>original: "Seelen-Geist," Böhme's specific term for the active, willing faculty of the soul that survives death.</note> Therefore, it is necessary for us to strive for something good, wherein the soul can spend its eternal play and have its joy; for the works of our soul follow us, and the works of the hands and of the outward spirit remain in this world. <note>original: "Spiel," which Böhme uses to describe the harmonious, creative activity of the divine or the redeemed soul.</note> For the soul is in eternity; whatever it makes and fashions for itself here stands forever before it—unless it breaks it down again. In that case, it is like a broken work which the soul no longer seeks, for it has moved on from it. For the Eternal carves an eternal model, and the fragile and beginning carves a fragile model; for after this time, all things will stand, each in its own model; for what the eternal will grasps receives an unbreakable form, provided the will itself does not break it.

# Chapter 12. Of Man.

[...Life] choose the best, in which he may have eternal joy: For if you were to choose beauty and honor for yourself, or wealth, you are then unworthy of your brother and sister, who are in misery in this world. For the beauty of this world despises the simple, and wealth squeezes the sweat out of the wretched, and great power pushes and oppresses the lowly and miserable: Great honor despises the simple, and does not equate itself with the needy. <note>original: "albere," meaning those who are plain, simple-hearted, or lacking in worldly cleverness and status.</note>

4. Thus, since in that [other] life many simple, miserable, and—in this world—despised, poor, weary souls will appear, their forms will not contain much highness, beauty, or desire for power and honor: For their souls have enclosed themselves in this vale of tears <term>vale of tears: (German: Jammerthal) a traditional Christian metaphor for the hardships of earthly life compared to the joy of heaven.</term> only within the gentle love of God, and have surrendered themselves to the simple and lowly, and dared to have no fellowship with power, splendor, and great honors, for these never equated themselves with them.

5. And since it is so, that the souls in that life shall have joy with one another, and each rejoice in the other's gifts and virtues; and yet the soul's essence gathered here in its eternal will shall appear as a figure; <note>original: "Figur," referring to the spiritual "form" or "signature" the soul carves out for itself through its desires and actions on earth.</note> so this is truly glorious and heartfelt for us to consider, that we should not embrace splendor and pride, nor greed and the oppression of the wretched, in our hearts in this world: For with all this we cannot enter into the community of Christ, they will not take us into their company, for it is a contrary thing.

6. In the Kingdom of Heaven there is nothing but love and harmony: each one assigns their love and favor to the other, and each rejoices in the other’s gifts, power, and beauty, which they have obtained from the Majesty of God; and they all thank God the Father in Christ Jesus, that He has chosen and accepted them as children, for the mighty power of the strong rejoices in the weak, that God’s Spirit is also in him, so that he also exists within the wonders in the eternal (single) will.

7. Therefore, dear children and brothers in Christ, let us enclose our hearts, minds, and wills in humility, in one love in this world, that we may yet be one in Christ.

<summary>Böhme argues that earthly status, wealth, and pride are incompatible with the Kingdom of Heaven, which is defined by mutual love and humility. He emphasizes that the "simple" and "miserable" of this world will find a community in Christ that the proud cannot enter.</summary>

### III. Of the Threefold Life, Chapter 12.

...in Christ. <note>original: "sto," the conclusion of "Christo" from the previous page.</note> If you are highly exalted in power, authority, and honor, then be humble; do not despise the simple and the wretched. Think that in that [other] life they will be in a high state alongside you. Do not squeeze the oppressed, and do not grieve the sorrowful, so that such things do not take hold of his soul and bar the gates of heaven to you. If you are beautiful of body, be not proud, and do not despise him who is not your equal, so that the soul of your simple brother or sister does not feel a loathing for you and cast you out of their mind. Be humble, so that your brother and sister may rejoice in you and bring your beauty to the praise of God, who has created such a beautiful, modest, and humble creature; be modest and friendly in words and works. You rich man, let your little streams flow into the house of the wretched, so that his soul may bless you. You powerful man, do not bend the law to please the mighty, so that the oppressed may bless you in your justice; in this way, you are also in the community of Christ. If you are high-ranking, do not allow your heart room to fly away in pride; humble yourself into the community of Christ, then the community will bless you and take you into their love.

8. Oh, how well it goes for the rich and powerful when the lowly and simple community of Christ loves him and wishes for God's salvation! Oh, how well it goes for a teacher and preacher who is a true servant of Christ, who gives his little sheep entrusted to him the food and drink of Christ, and refreshes them with it, so that their souls give themselves to his obedience and love him from the heart, wishing him all well-being! Oh, how blessed and shining is he in Christ! What a truly beautiful shepherd is he, for his sheep follow him, and he leads them to the Chief Shepherd! <note>original: "Ertz-Hirten," referring to Christ as the Arch-Shepherd or Great Shepherd.</note> Oh, how poorly he stands, whom they—rightfully and in truth—curse; from him the beautiful garment of Christ is taken away, and he puts on a mask of vice. <term>mask of vice: (German: Laster-Larve) an outward appearance or persona shaped by sin rather than the divine image.</term> But he who is cursed for the sake of righteousness breaks out like gold from the stone and puts on Christ's crown of martyrdom, in which all holy souls will greatly rejoice on that day—that he remained a steadfast disciple of Christ, who did not look upon honor and power, or money and property, but has rightly pastured Christ's sheep.

### III. Of the Threefold Life, Chapter 12.

12. If we lift up our heart to Him and surrender ourselves to Him in obedience, then we are all within His will, and no one can thrust us out of it. We all stand here in this life in one field and grow, and the stars and the elements are the field in which we grow. God has sown us into it; Adam is the first grain that God Himself sowed, and from that same grain we all grow. We are all of one seed; we are altogether brothers and sisters in the body. But the devil has sown weeds <note>A reference to the Parable of the Tares (Matthew 13), where an enemy sows weeds among the wheat.</note> between and among us. He has not sown humans, for that he cannot do in all eternity; rather, he has blinded us and has sown **pride**, **envy**, **wrath**, **greed**, and **evil will** into our minds <term>Gemüthe: the deep, emotional and spiritual core of a person</term>, so that he might destroy us. For he begrudges us the honor of being God’s children in his place, where he once was; he fell from God through wrath, pride, and envy, and turned away from God. Therefore, he wishes to seduce us so that only his kingdom might become great.

13. O dear children of God! Trust him <note>Referring to the devil.</note> not, for wherever God sows His good seed, the devil follows after and sows weeds into it. Then He will give us rain and blessing in body and soul, and after this life, He will take us to Himself into His kingdom, where we shall all be eternally redeemed from our tribulation.

14. Thus, and in no other way, is the teaching of Moses and all the Prophets, and also of Christ: that we should love one another as one life, and God in us. ### III. Of the Threefold Life, Chapter 12.

...striven for **God**. The dear martyrs, who have seen the light of **God**, will not reject you from their congregation because of this, since you did not recognize such things, but were led so blindly.

19. Look and take note of what the zealous will can accomplish when a person enters into **God’s** will with all their desires; and even if they do not yet know it, and are zealous in a foreign opinion <note>original: *Meinung*; Böhme uses this term to refer to sectarian dogmas, human-made religious theories, or literalist interpretations that lack spiritual depth</note>, their heart is nevertheless directed toward **God**, and they believe quite firmly in their ignorance that it pleases **God** so. Within such opinions, great wonders and deeds occurred under the Antichrist’s kingdom, for nothing is impossible to a strong faith. The Antichrist wrapped himself in these wonders and created almost as many opinions as there are days in the year; and since wonders also occurred among the believers who believed thus in blindness within their opinion, the Antichrist attributed this to the "opinion" itself. Yet the opinion never moved even a gnat. Rather, it was the firm and strong faith, which passed through the opinion into **God**, that awakened the wonders. For the Spirit of **God** is in faith, and not in the opinion, and faith is from **God**; for the soul directs itself through the opinion toward **God** and seizes **God’s** Spirit. The opinion is the fire, but the soul does not remain in the fire; rather, it breaks through into **God** and blooms out of the fire like a beautiful flower (out of the earth).

20. These opinions were to be tolerated in **God**, and **God** did not reject them, as long as the soul sought **God** through the opinion, and as long as the Church of Christ stood under one governance <note>original: *Regiment*; referring to the spiritual administration, order, or authority of the church</note>. But when the devil locked himself into it and made a glittering kingdom for himself out of it—so that the priests sought only honor, greed, and lust within it, and led people away from **God** merely into their own works <note>original: *Wercke*; here meaning religious rituals or "good works" performed as empty obligations rather than from inner faith</note>—then the opinions became completely blind. For they themselves departed from **God** into the works of their own hands, into invented paths. Therefore, **God** also let them go, since they would not allow themselves to be drawn by His Spirit.

21. And Asia and Africa, as well as Greece, are to be considered blessed for this reason: that they have departed from human works and entered again into the One **God**. ### III. Of the Threefold Life, Chapter 12.

...remained in the **one God**, and they in harmony; for people did not then so violently revile and blaspheme for the sake of the precious name of **Christ** as those have done who were led blindly in the darkness of their works. They have not only reviled those who deviated from them, but they themselves have bitten and blasphemed each other in their "opinions" <note>original: *Meinungen*; Böhme uses this term to describe sectarian dogmas or human-made religious theories that lack true spiritual life</note> like a dog over a bone, and have misled the layman, who goes groping in the dark and knows not which opinion is best: thus you cling to the opinion and are perjured to **God**.

22. When the simple person must die, he knows not where he should commit his soul; he clings to his works and to the opinion, and leaves the will of **God**, and so remains outside of **God**. Where do you think, then, that the poor soul remains when it is outside **God's** will? Behold, we will tell you, for we know this for certain; for the Spirit of our Mother <note>Böhme refers here to Divine Wisdom or the "Maternal" generative power of God that reveals hidden truths</note> reveals this to us, so that we see with both eyes.

23. **Christ** says: *Where your treasure is, there also is your heart* (Matthew 6:21). Behold, the soul is wrapped up in the "opinion" and runs with it to the patron <note>original: *Patron*; likely referring to a patron saint or the leader of a specific religious sect</note> who taught it so, and seeks him; and if it does not find him, it becomes sorrowful and has no rest, hovering thus between heaven and hell, and would gladly escape the devil.

24. Therefore it has come to pass that poor souls have often appeared again in the congregation, or otherwise in houses, fields, and churches, and called to the congregation for help with their prayers, and entered into the [religious] orders, thinking thus to receive relief. This is how the concept of Purgatory <note>original: *Feg-Feuer*; literally "scouring-fire" or "cleansing fire"</note> was created. For the soul truly experiences Purgatory if it cannot reach **God's** will; and yet, in such fervent surrender to these opinions, some have sunk through the opinion into **God** and thus reached the silent eternity. We mean, however, those souls who have imagined <term>imagined: in Böhme’s vocabulary, *imaginiret* refers to the soul’s power to "form" its own reality or internal state</term> the Kingdom of **God** through their opinions, and not the souls of the deceivers <note>original: *Triegers*; those who use religion for personal gain or manipulation</note> who sought their own profit and pleasure therein. Those deceivers are all to play the harlot with the Antichrist, for they are bound to him by oath; and even if they sit in hellish fire with him to play the harlot, they still flatter him and blaspheme **God**, as if He were doing them an injustice.

### III. Of the Threefold Life Chapter 13.

...that one sees the human creature standing palpably and comprehensibly in Heaven, in the same form as He was here on Earth. You see nothing more of Him than the **Majesty of the Clarity of the Radiance**, which fills the Angelic world. And wherever the Majesty is, there is Christ's **Essence** <note>original: *Wesenheit*. In Böhme's mystical theology, this refers to "heavenly corporeality"—a spiritual substance that is more real than physical matter.</note>; for the Heart and Word of God have married into that Essence. Just as you think that the Word is everywhere, so too is the Essence of the Word's body, though without a fixed shape; for only the **Creature** <note>The specific individual form or being, in this case, the person of Christ.</note> possesses the [distinct] formation.

19. I give you an analogy: Behold, all things are created from Water, and in the Water was all power; for you find that everything has Water [within it], even if it is a stone, it is still Water, whether it be flesh or whatever it may be; but the **Sulfur** <note>original: *Sulphur*. An alchemical term used by Böhme to describe the active, formative "spirit" or "oil" within matter that allows it to take shape and burn with life.</note> is within it with the power of Nature, which forms the essence. Now see, in the entire Depth there is nothing but Water, Air, and Fire; from these three, essence comes to be, such as body or earth. Now you surely see that the single Sun causes this; it is also the power and majesty in this elemental essence. Everything belongs to the Sun, and everything desires the Sun, and the Sun provides the governance with its power.

20. See, think of it in this analogy: God is the eternal Sun in the **second Principle** <note>original: *Principio*. Böhme divided existence into three "Principles": the dark fire-source (Father), the light-world of love (Son), and the external physical world.</note>—understand this as the Heart, Radiance, Power, and Majesty. And the elements of Fire, Water, and Earth are God the Father, speaking here by way of analogy. Now the Sun stands there as a **Body** <note>original: *Corpus*.</note>, which indeed it is; that signifies the Creature of Christ. And the whole essence of the four elements in all directions signifies the essence of the creature in which the Sun's radiance shines: the Sun signifies the Word and the Majesty, and the four elements signify the power of the body, and the Father, from whom the Son shines forth.

21. Therefore know, that the Father’s power is everywhere in Heaven, and in that power is the Word, and the Word has essence; all of this belongs to the person of Christ. For Christ stands in His Father like an image, just as the Sun stands in the elements. If God wished to reveal Himself, the whole world would be nothing but Sun, for the Depth catches the radiance of the Sun. Otherwise, if there were no such essence in the Depth like the Sun is, it would not catch the light; thus it only desires its like. It is the same in Heaven.

We are gods, if we remain in Him: He is the fountain, our light, and we are His stars; He gives us His body and power, and His radiance for our light. Thus He feeds us here on earth in the **Lord’s Supper** <note>original: *Abendmahl*. Referring to the Eucharist or Holy Communion.</note>—whenever we desire it—with the power of His body and with the Spirit from that power, for that same spirit is the power’s spirit and life. Sulfur is the Father’s property; the essentiality is the body, and the Sulfur has power, and in that power is the light of life, as another person. And from the power in the light, the **breath** <note>original: *Ruch*. An archaic term for scent or breath, here referring to the Holy Spirit.</note> and spirit of the power goes out; it cannot be grasped or held by the power, yet it proceeds from the power: that is the Holy Spirit of God.

23. Therefore, understand us correctly: in the Lord’s Supper, we do not receive another creature with a new soul. The soul eats Christ’s flesh and drinks His blood, which fills the heavens; and from that which the soul receives and eats, a body grows for it. In that same body, the soul is in God’s hand and can, at the end of the world, pass through the fire of God’s wrath with that same body without feeling it. Just as that same fire cannot seize Christ in the Trinity, it likewise cannot seize us; for the fire receives **gentleness** <note>original: *Sanftmuth*.</note> from God’s gentleness and our own, and is transformed within us into a rising of the desire of love, so that our fire and burning within us is a pure desire for love; for it becomes a radiance of **Majesty**, and thus we are in God and God’s children. Hallelujah, Hallelujah, Hallelujah!

36. What do you seek so much, you wild branches? You say, "We are above the mother; we possess wit and art." What does the mother care for your wit and art?
