### Chapter 13. Of Mankind.

Knowledge is your snare that entangles you; if you were simple-minded <note>original: *alber*. In Böhme’s era, this term carried the sense of being "simple," "innocent," or "naive" rather than its modern German meaning of "silly."</note>, you would not be so proud. What does the simple person know of false cunning and deceit, if they did not learn it from the knowledge of the **Turmoil** <note>original: *Turbæ*. The Latin term *Turba* refers to the chaotic, destructive force of God’s wrath that arises when creatures turn away from divine unity into multiplicity and pride.</note>?

38. You say, "We carry God's will and teach it." Are you not Cain, who murders Abel every day? Just look at yourself properly, for you are indeed him: Abel lies at your feet and pleads with you, but you are the evil beast that treads Abel underfoot; you ride over bent knees and regard the simple man as dust, yet you devour the fruit of his sweat <note>An expression referring to the exploitation of the labor and survival of the poor.</note> and fill yourself with groundless deceit. How then can you say: "Here is the Church of Christ!"? Oh, you are Babylon, a city of whoredom and falsehood. You know God’s will, but you do only your own will, and you even say, "We have come out of Babylon, we have the true teaching with us." Truly, if you had the spirit of righteousness and truth and were satisfied with a little, the Mother <note>The "Mother" represents the divine wisdom and the sustaining source of the soul.</note> would always give you enough; you would suffer no lack. But your splendor and pride do not trust God; therefore you rely only on greed <note>original: *Geiß*, an archaic form of *Geiz* (avarice).</note> and wish only to gorge yourself alone on the fat of the earth; you take it by force and not by right. The "right" that you uphold has been concocted by your false, greedy heart; you live only in deceit. You persuade and deceive yourself to your own ruin; if you were truly wise, you would look toward your end and what follows after this life. But you blind yourself with pride and yet say: "Here is the golden time; many would have loved to see what we see and hear what we hear, yet they neither saw nor heard it." <note>An ironic use of Matthew 13:17. Böhme suggests that while people boast of living in an era of great revelation, their behavior makes them more guilty than their ancestors.</note> Yes, listen: it shall also be a testimony against you and make your judgment all the heavier. Up to now, you have not become better, but worse; therefore know that what was proclaimed to you was your own prophet, who called you back from your pride into the Mother of Humility; but you have only grown worse, you have broken the Spirit’s sword so that you may do whatever you want. But He has forsaken you and handed you over to the **Turmoil**, which shall devour you, just as happened to Israel in ancient times. No counsel helps, your alliances are all in vain; because you rely on the arm of flesh, God has also departed from you and lets you proceed, so that you consume yourself.

### III. Of the Threefold Life Chapter 14.

39. Or why do you take the Covenant of God into your mouth, while you yet hate discipline and seek only greed? <note>original: *Geiſs*. The chaotic, destructive force of God’s wrath that breaks things apart when they turn away from divine unity.</term> drives it; the Turmoil has its delight in fulfilling the wrath of God, devouring what has grown in His kingdom. Yet you are blind to this and do not see it. Why do you boast so much? Simply go out from it! Do you not see how the noble **Tincture** <term>original: *Tinctur*. In Böhme’s alchemy-influenced theology, this is the spiritual life-force or "essence" that transforms and ennobles base matter into spiritual "gold."</term> has raised itself up? It will very soon give its flower; then you shall have enough silver and gold.

40. But what should one say? You have heard yourself while sleeping: you would rather go down alive into the **Abyss** <note>original: *Abgrund*. Therefore, that which your own prophet <note>Likely a reference to Martin Luther or a general prophetic warning of the Reformation era.</note> shows you—who has long been calling to you with his trumpet—shall surely come to pass. You only wait for the sword of fire, and that sword will indeed cut you. Or do you think we are mad to speak this way? Indeed: we are born out of you, and we see and understand the lament of our Mother <note>The "Mother" represents the divine Wisdom or the natural soul of the world grieving for her children.</note> who punishes her children; for she points out the grimness in the Turmoil, which has grown even into the fierce wrath of God. We speak what is given to us, what we recognize in the zeal of the Lord. What have we to do with **Babylon** <note>original: *Babel*. Represents the "city of confusion," the state of fragmented, sectarian, and worldly religion.</note>? We speak with ourselves, and with the members of our own body, and with those who dwell in the **Courts of God**, who are now sorrowful with us—a sorrow that shall be turned into joy.

### 1.
Dear children of God, let us consider heartily and most inwardly from whence we are, or where we want to go: And then, what we do and intend, so that we do not lose the eternal and highest good.

2. Why do we strive so much after temporal pleasure, after honor, money and goods? After all, we are only foreign guests in this life and pilgrims as well, who must wait every hour for when this life ends. We were not created for the pleasure of this life, but for paradisiacal joy, and for a simple, childlike life: We should know of no pomp or pride; but live together as children in a game of joy. We have gone out from our right, pure, paradisiacal mother, in whom we should live as dear children: We are enclosed in the mother who gives birth to the evil beasts <note>A reference to the material, fallen world or "Mother Nature" in its corrupted state.</note>, and have received an animal-like quality <term>thierische Eigenschaft: the carnal, instinctive nature of man that prioritizes survival and appetite over the spirit.</term>. Do you think Christ’s body and blood dwell in the earthly element in such a way that you can grasp it with your teeth? Oh no, friend! She must be in **GOD'S** will if she wishes to eat of **GOD**: she can also eat of Christ’s flesh at every hour, if she lives in Christ’s flesh; for every spirit eats of its own body.

### Ch. 14. Of Man.

...and goes forth, which dwells in the <term>Tincture <note>original: "Tinctur"; in Böhme’s philosophy, this is the spiritual life-blood or essence that bridges the spiritual and physical worlds.</note></term>, is the eternal life of the soul; and the spirit of desire, with the quality of the <term>stellar dominion <note>original: "Sternen-Regiment"; the astrological influence of the stars and planets that Böhme believed governed the physical body and earthly impulses.</note></term>, is the beginning and the ending, fragile life; that is, the animal life.

33. Now the soul is born only from the first two <note>Referring to the first two "Principles" or foundations of existence: the dark fire-source and the light-source of God's majesty.</note>, and the third was breathed into it: not so that it should enter therein and surrender itself to it, as it did in Adam, but that it should rule mightily over it and reveal within it the great wonders of **GOD**, which have been foreseen from eternity in the Wisdom of **GOD**; for the third dominion was born and created out of the first. And the other dominion was meant to remain in its seat, in the noble Tincture in Paradise, and was meant to reveal the great wonders in the third: therefore man was a master over all things; he held the Tincture of the earth in his hand, and gold and silver would have been as easy for him to find as other visible things. The Tincture of the earth was his ornament and play, everything childlike without [earthly] spirit: no other clothing was necessary for him; just as gold is pure without blemish, so also was his childlike <term>mind <note>original: "Gemüthe"; the deep seat of the soul's will and emotions.</note></term>. But the devil awakened <term>Sulphur <note>original: "Sulphur"; here used to mean the combustible, harsh, and restless property of material nature.</note></term> within it, and set the animal spirit as the over-ruler, over which man was meant to rule; that same spirit now rules over him, and that is his Fall.

34. Thus the devil has now gained power: because the outer dominion is born from the inner, and he dwells in the inner, he slips from the inner into the outer and inflames the outer in the mind; from this arises the false craving and evil desire, so that two dominions now struggle against the dominion of the soul. And the poor soul is in the midst, between the dominion of this world and the dominion of hellish torment; there it stands before the <term>Gates of Heaven <note>original: "Himmels-Porten"</note></term> in a great depth, in great danger. Its root is **GOD’S** wrath and the hellish fire, and its over-spirit is the dominion of this world; there it stands in the midst in the <term>Fire-Tincture <note>The soul’s fundamental energetic state before it is transformed by light.</note></term>: whichever way it reaches, into that it enters. If it reaches into the lust of this world, then it stands therein and is captured by the devil; but if it reaches into itself, into **GOD**, then the devil strikes at it, for the soul is now in his territory. ### III. Of the Threefold Life Ch. 14.

...his country: that is a tree to him, which is his poison and death; he is hostile to it and does not like to touch it; but he incites his servants against the outer body, which must bear shame and mockery, so that he may indeed cover this tree so that it is not recognized. He fears it might otherwise produce more little branches, and ultimately hell might become too narrow for him; therefore he resists as long as he can.

35. Now, when the poor soul breaks away from him and turns with her dear Bridegroom Christ toward **GOD’S** love—entering into **GOD’S** will through earnest repentance and turning back into **GOD**—he still has seven snares <note>original: "Fallstricke"; these represent the entrapments of the material and selfish nature.</note> with which he holds her before he lets her go. There she must wind herself free through all seven, leaving him nothing but his ropes. At the eighth, she must go through the fire; that is the earnest trial <note>original: "Proba"; the Refiner’s fire or spiritual test of faith.</note>. And when she comes through there, she attains the heavenly <term>Tincture <note>The spiritual essence or "life-blood" that transforms the soul from a base state to a divine one.</note></term> in the ninth number; and in the tenth number at the cross <note>The original uses the symbol "†e" to represent the Cross/Kreuz.</note> she attains Christ’s body, so that she is an angel in heaven and a guest on earth in this valley of tabernacles <note>original: "Hütten Thal"; a reference to the temporary, fragile nature of earthly life.</note>.

36. The seven ropes with which the soul is bound are the seven spirits of external nature—the government of this world—through which she must wind and penetrate, casting them all behind her. And in the eighth number stands Moses with his Law, where it is first read to the soul what a beautiful bird she once was; there the devil comes with his register <note>A record or ledger of the soul's sins.</note> and reads to her what she is, asserting his right to her. Then the word is: bow down and grasp the wounds and the suffering of **JESUS CHRIST**. Here it is necessary that the poor sinner takes the merit and death of Christ and wraps herself firmly within them; for the devil cannot tear the soul out of these swaddling clothes, nor does he dare to touch them. In this place, the devil must leave the soul, for Christ stands in the Father’s fire of wrath and is the fulfillment of obedience. There, the soul is led into the ninth number, into the Tincture of eternal life; there she is embraced by **GOD’S** majesty, and the beautiful, gracious <term>Virgin of the Wisdom of GOD <note>Sophia, or Divine Wisdom, depicted by Böhme as a feminine spiritual guide and the soul's true mirror.</note></term> meets her with her crown of pearls and crowns the soul as a Knight of Heaven <note>original: "Himmels-Ritter".</note>.

### III. Of the Threefold Life Ch. 14.

...[to] write, nor otherwise do we have a mouth in this world to speak such things. We only wish for the reader and all people that they might experience it for themselves, for which reason we proceed with much toil and deep labor in this writing; for we write what we ourselves have recognized and seen with spiritual eyes. We do not say this for our own glory, but so that the reader may know what to expect if they wish to follow after us; since they otherwise see that the world views **GOD’S** children as nothing but an owl <note>To be seen as an "owl" (Eule) is a metaphor for being a target of mockery or perceived as a strange creature of the night by those who live in the "daylight" of worldly reason.</note>; but we wish to delight ourselves well after this short life. Thus, this little wreath <note>original: "Kränzlein"; Böhme often uses the image of a floral wreath or crown to symbolize the spiritual breakthrough and the "bloom" of the soul in God’s light.</note> is dearer to us than the whole world, even though it is sometimes hidden from us; yet it does not die. For just as the harsh winter covers the green earth, where reason says, "everything is dead," but when spring returns, it begins to turn green and bloom; so it is also with the noble and beautiful little wreath of Christ: when it greens again, it brings forth lilies without number, and every spring—whenever the mind is renewed in Christ—it returns tenfold.

### Of the Attendance of the Holy Angels.

38. As we humans here in this world—provided we are indeed children of **GOD**—come to one another’s aid in need and accident, and gladly rescue one another from suffering and tribulation, so it is also with the children of **GOD** in heaven. Since the soul belongs to the company of angels, they gladly stay close to God-fearing, pious, and modest people, and stand by them in times of need. For the Scripture also says: They are all ministering spirits sent out to serve those who shall inherit the kingdom of **GOD**. They very often catch the fiery rays of the **Evil One**. What misfortune would the devil not often cause on earth if he were not resisted by the Prince-Thrones <note>original: "Thron-Fürsten"; a reference to the high-ranking celestial hierarchy (Thrones) mentioned in traditional angelology.</note> of the legions? How often would he terrify and overthrow people? But the angels are our servants and guardians—provided we are Christians and not animals <note>Böhme uses "animals" or "beasts" to describe humans who live only by their earthly, carnal instincts without spiritual awareness.</note>—even though the devil pursues Christians most of all. How very often many a person would drown, or fall to their death, who instead receives a wonderful rescue from the angels. They love to be around people who sing and speak of **GOD**; they take their joy with the innocent <note>original: "unmündigen"; literally "the minor" or "those without a voice," referring to young children or the simple-hearted.</note>...

### III. Of the Threefold Life Ch. 14.

...to young children, so that they may even reveal themselves to a child and play with them, provided it is a child of **GOD**. How very many examples are contained in Holy Scripture showing that the angels have guided and led pious children—especially the example of Tobias, which our school-rabbis <note>The "school-rabbis" refers to the academic theologians of Böhme's day who were often skeptical of the Apocrypha, such as the Book of Tobit, and sought to remove them from the biblical canon.</note> would rather cast out of the Bible. Behold the labor at His birth, and with the Wise Men from the East, and finally with Joseph, how he was to lead Mary with the infant into Egypt. In this, we can well perceive their great care for us, for they are **GOD’S** servants; He sends them to guide us and protect us from the devil. What great joy they have with a poor soul when it is torn from the devil’s snares—more than for ninety-nine who are righteous, as Christ says in Luke 15:7.

39. Therefore, we should not tremble so in tribulation when we are in need, often thinking the whole world is against us; for the angelic host is with us, and the Spirit of **GOD**. It often goes with us as it did with the Canaanite woman <note>A reference to the woman in Matthew 15:21–28 who persisted in her faith even when it seemed Jesus was ignoring her; Böhme uses her as a model for enduring spiritual "trials."</note>, when we cannot find **GOD’S** face; but we must stand firm, for we must be tried and proven. The more one purifies gold, the more beautiful and clear it becomes. So it is also with the soul: the more it is led into the trial, if it stands firm, the more beautiful and clear it becomes. And **GOD** is concerned with this because He wishes to have beautiful, dear children who become wise and learn to know the old devil.

40. But know this: the angels are entirely pure, chaste, and modest spirits, and moreover humble and friendly; they resemble innocent children who know of no falsehood, except what is innate to them. Whoever wishes to enjoy the company of angels and have them as traveling companions must not be a lustful bull, nor carry a wanton Venus <note>original: "geile Venus"; Böhme uses the Roman goddess of love as a symbol for carnal lust and worldly desire which drives away the holy angels.</note> or a false mind that plots only craftiness and deceit day and night, seeking how to gain property and status. He must also not bathe himself every hour in the world’s clever, jesting words, tickling his soul with them and—

There it must step earnestly into humility, thus treading upon the devil’s head and destroying his hell. Then the angels approach the person and have great joy that he who presumed to be God and Creator in the soul has been overcome.

But when the soul casts away the evil desire, he is driven out by the angel, and there is a constant struggle for the soul of man: **GOD** wants to have it, and the devil wants to have it too. And this is the cause of the struggle, that two kingdoms divide upon the cross: one is **GOD’S** love, the kingdom in the <term>Holy Ternary [Ternario Sancto]</term> <note>original: "Ternario Sancto"; Böhme's term for the holy, manifested realm of the Trinity in the spiritual world.</note>, which is the angelic realm; and the other is the fierce wrath from the <term>Center of Nature [Centro Naturæ]</term> <note>original: "Centro Naturæ"; the fundamental root of existence which contains the potential for both light and darkness.</note>, which is **GOD’S** wrath and severity.

44. Therefore, **GOD** has revealed His will to us and presented light and darkness to man; he may reach for whichever he wants. And so that we may recognize that He wants to have the soul in His Holy Kingdom, He allows us to be taught and shows us the way to life. Through His Spirit, He awakens precious teachers who are the light of the world, so that men should guard themselves against His wrath and fierce anger, and not awaken it within themselves. If we instead make ourselves into a fierce, angry, false, and high-flying devil who flies out beyond all love and gentleness into sheer greed, hunger, and thirst, then we are that too. ## Chapter 15.

### Of the Mixed World and its Wickedness: How it stands now, and how it conducts its rule; a mirror in which everyone may look and examine themselves, to see what spirit's child they are: from the Mirror of Wonders (Seal). <note>The "Mirror of Wonders" refers to Böhme’s concept of the Divine Wisdom (Sophia) acting as a reflective surface in which the wonders of God and the states of the soul are revealed.</note>

Everyone runs after the greedy whore <note>A reference to the biblical "Whore of Babylon," representing worldly greed and spiritual corruption.</note>, who is full of vice and abomination; the shepherd does this along with his sheep. It is a most sorrowful time, and if it were not shortened, no human would be saved. This is a time of which all the prophets have prophesied, and yet you think it is a golden age.

3. Look at yourself, you blind human: where have you gone? Do you think that this wickedness and falsehood you practice is God’s order? Just wait for the time; you will soon see it. It is the time of the last seal, when the wrath of God has poured out its bowls, so that the wonders of hell come to light. Let this be told to you; we have recognized it in the <term>Holy Ternary</term> <note>original: "Ternario Sancto." In Böhme's philosophy, this refers to the "Holy Threefoldness" or the manifested divine world where the three principles of God's being are in harmony.</note>. For the Mother has rejected this and wants the abominations no more; she is pregnant and gives birth to a son in her old age, who shortens the days of wickedness. Let this be told to you: whoever persists in his wickedness will have great shame from it.

4. Even the little boy, running about in children's games, is now full of the poison and malice of the devil, and all the vices of wickedness stick within him. He is a mocker and a blasphemer, moreover a curser, a swearer, and a deceiver, quite well-prepared to serve the devil in all shameful vices. Unchastity is the "Latin" on his tongue <note>A metaphor meaning that crude or immoral speech is the language he has mastered most fluently, just as scholars mastered Latin.</note>; he knows how to inflict all sorts of scornful, jesting words upon the simple-minded. All manner of theft is a skill to him; deception is a point of pride. They mock pious people without a second thought; whoever fears God must be their fool and "owl" <note>To be an "owl" (Eule) was a contemporary idiom for being a target of mockery or a social outcast.</note>. The elders see this and take their joy and pleasure in the fact that their child is so "skilled" in such decadence. They tickle their hearts with it when their children mock honest people; what they themselves dare not carry out, they teach their children, so that they may fulfill the lust of their hearts. The devil teaches them all of this; he rides in their hearts as a master over soul and body.

5. Whoever can deceive, slander, and betray his neighbor, and strip him of honor and goods, takes his pleasure in it. All unchaste words and gestures are considered...

6. Youth first learns the devil’s craft before they learn to earn anything else, among both the male and female sex. Despicable, mocking, and malicious extravagance <note>original: "Uppigkeit" — this carries connotations of luxury, pride, and wantonness.</note> is the first work they learn, to which the parents faithfully assist, considering it a worldly art and exercise. When they have grown a little older, the desire for beastly unchastity is the second work they learn, and one entices the other to it. Youth surrenders the heart to the devil immediately in its first bloom, so that the devil may build his net (nest) within it, catching one person through the abominations of another: the man with the woman, and the woman with the man.

7. If a man sends a son to the university <note>original: "hohe Schule" — literally "high school," but referring to the university in this period.</note> so that he might learn something good, and be useful to God and the world, he instead learns extravagance, pride, and cunning—how one might wrest from a simple person his own property and the fruit of his sweat through trickery. They wrap a cloak around it and call it **law** <note>original: "Jura" — Latin for "laws" or legal studies.</note>; but the cloak belongs to the devil, and the false heart is his servant. If he knows a few foreign languages, then no simple man is good enough for him anymore; his pride soars above all. This stinking bag of maggots <note>original: "Madensack" — a blunt, common Reformation-era term for the physical, mortal body, emphasizing its eventual decay.</note> must be draped in fine cloths and tassels. These are people who can act refined until they push the "gnawing worm" <note>A metaphor for the "worm of conscience" or the lasting sting of shame and sorrow, often following seduction.</note> into the heart of many a mother’s daughter.

8. Such people are placed in charge of churches and schools: they are supposed to be Christ’s shepherds, and yet they have the devil as a guest in their hearts. How will you answer for your office, into which you were placed so that you should resist injustice and keep the godless in the constraint of punishment? ### III. Of the Threefold Life, Chapter 15.

To such a person, it is powerful and useful; but the hypocrites only use it for appearance, so that they may bear the name of Christians. Yet, they carry the name of God in vain and shall give a solemn account for it.

16. O you **Antichristian shepherds** <note>Böhme frequently used this term to describe the established clergy of his time, whom he believed valued dogma and social status over spiritual rebirth.</note> of the new order! You who cover the hypocrite and false deceiver with the suffering of Christ through false hypocrisy—to please the favor of men and for the sake of your **idol belly** <note>original: "Abgott Bauchs"; a biblical reference to those whose god is their own appetite or material greed.</note>—though he is only a "name-only" Christian: how will you answer for this when Christ demands His sheep from you? You have knowingly tucked wolves under His purple mantle, wherein the devil dwells. Why do you not crack open the nut in which the kernel and the heart lie? Why do you not proclaim his abominations to the high and the low alike? If you are Christ's shepherds, why do you not act as Christ did, who set the truth before everyone’s eyes? He shattered and He healed, not for the sake of favor or any person's reputation, but according to His Father's will. That is what Christ’s shepherds are also bound to do.

17. You, dear **Reason** <term>Vernunft: the earthly, logical intellect that Böhme distinguishes from "Understanding" (Verstand), which is spiritually illuminated.</term>, you walk quite wisely upon the streets of this world as far as the external body is concerned; but where does the poor soul remain? Truly, it is not at home in this life; this is not its eternal fatherland. What does it help you to have a little while of **pleasure** <note>original: "Wollust"; implies worldly or sensual delight at the expense of spiritual health.</note> with eternal loss? Or what does it matter if you let your children strut about in this world for a little while and take delight in it, when they despise the wretched—and you lose them afterward eternally? You think you love them and are doing them well; when the world praises their cunning, luxury, and falsehood or roguery, that praise pleases you. But the devil takes that up, and you are the murderer of your children; you are their greatest enemy. For children look to their parents: when their antics please the parents, they practice them all the more and are all the bolder. At the **Last Judgment**, they will cry out against their parents for not turning them away from luxury and a godless life (existence) and toward discipline and the fear of God.

18. Do you love your life and your children? Then lose them... <note>Referring to the Gospel paradox: "Whoever finds their life will lose it, and whoever loses their life for my sake will find it."</note>

It will happen that he thinks he is alone on the path: but God always has His 7,000 beside him, as with Elijah <note>A reference to 1 Kings 19:18, where God tells the prophet Elijah that he is not the only faithful one left.</note>, whom he does not recognize. Böhme suggests the believer is so focused on their own flaws that they cannot see their own spiritual progress.</term>, in which the devil fights against him; that is always before him. But his holiness he does not know in this world, for Christ hides it under His **cross** <note>The "Cross" represents the trials and humility of the believer's earthly life, which serves as a protective veil over their spiritual transformation to keep them from pride.</note>, so that the devil does not see it. Therefore, be alert and cheerful, and resist the cunning devil, so that you may live eternally.

### The Very Lovely Gate.

A hungry spirit, which is exhausted and weary, is desiring of quiet gentleness and rest, so that it may depart from the torment of the driver <note>The "driver" (Treiber) refers to the restless, driving forces of the material world and the "Spiritus Mundi" that keep the soul in a state of anxiety.</note>, and satisfy itself with gentleness and silence, and then with that which is the desire of its life, from which it maintains its body.

2. Thus, my dear mind <term>mind: "Gemüthe" in Böhme's vocabulary refers to the seat of the soul's inclinations, will, and emotional disposition.</term>, you are born from the eternal quiet gentleness; you were in God's Wisdom before the times of the world: The gentleness of God’s love was your source <note>original: "Qual." Böhme uses this word to mean both "source/quality" and "torment," describing the churning energy of life.</note>, and you were a fruitful vine in your quiet eternal Mother, when you were not yet created as a spirit. This does not trouble the Father at all; He is joyful with His servants, the holy angels and holy souls, and lets the angry one—who refuses to share heavenly joy with his brother—go away into the wrath-pit of the Devil. And He is joyful with His child; but because the hypocrite is angry and despises the Father's supper <note>This refers to the "Abendmahl" or Holy Communion, which Böhme views here as a spiritual feast of the soul.</note>, he also does not enjoy the heavenly joys.

17. He is glad to have us. If you are our brother, why then do you grunt? If you are the Pope in the house, then look and be the Father’s obedient son, and rejoice with the lost son when he leaves the Antichrist to go to the Father. If you will not do that, then you must be angry eternally, and share no joy in eternity with us lost and revived children. So says the Spirit of the Great Wonders.

In Böhme's cosmology, the stars represent the macrocosmic forces of nature that influence the human soul and body.</note>, which must rest in the Spirit of Christ, also lust to possess such a heart and soul where God’s Spirit has resided, for all creatures long for the power of God. They have a wisdom and create the spirit of this world: indeed, they possess great art, for the **Great Mystery** <note>original: "Mysterium Magnum," the chaotic potential or "Great Chaos" from which the world was created.</note>—earthly and elemental—lies within them. But they do not have the key to the **Principle** <note>original: "Principio"</note> of the freedom of God outside of nature, for they have a beginning and an end, and see no further; they only create and seek a hypocritical, animal-like life.

23. Therefore, let us not be proud and secure, and let us not rely on art, much less on the letter <note>The "letter" refers to the literal text of the Bible without spiritual interpretation.</note>, for its Spirit is hidden from us without God’s Spirit: We have God’s will clearly in the Holy Scripture, but without God’s Spirit, we have only a husk and a dead word; God’s Spirit first awakens the living Word in us, so that we may understand the letter and the written word. This is shown clearly enough by the fact that the art-scholars are only letter-learned scholars <note>original: "Buchstaben-Gelehrte"</note>, and not those taught by God; otherwise, they would not quarrel over Christ’s honor and teaching, and would not dance so [recklessly] around the cup of Christ <note>likely a reference to the fierce theological disputes regarding the Eucharist/Lord's Supper.</note>.

24. Even if 1000 people taught by God, who are born in the Spirit of Christ, were together, and each had a special gift and recognition in God, they would still all be united in the root of Christ, and each would only desire the love of God in Christ: Which disciple will exalt himself over his master? If we are one body in Christ, why does one member need to quarrel with another over food? When the desiring mouth eats, all members receive strength; every member has its business to open up the wonders of God: We do not all carry one word, but one Spirit in Christ; to each is allotted his own [part] of what he should reveal in God, so that the great secrets of God might become manifest, and the wonders, which...

He has cleared the path for us so that we should follow Him in love and meekness, just as children should follow their parents. Therefore, He teaches us so faithfully what we should do and how we should pray.

Böhme suggests that true spiritual wonders only arise when the ego releases its hold.</note>, for letting is the bath. **Un** <note>The first syllable of *unsern* (our).</note>, this syllable, however, pierces into the love of God, and desires to lead the washed souls into love. **Sern** <note>The second syllable of *unsern*.</note>, this syllable points out before God the evil child, which is now washed in love, and presents it as one of God’s wonders: For it represents that which has come to a wonder out of the fire-tincture <term>original: "Feuers-Tinctur." The spiritual essence or "color" of the soul's inner fire; a key concept in alchemy and Böhme's theology.</term> in the soul. **Schul** <note>The first syllable of *Schuld* (debt/guilt).</note>, this syllable indicates the useless work that one soul has wrought against another out of the fire-tincture: And it is a representation of the evil, which the soul has washed and purified again in the will itself. **Di** <note>From *Schuldigern* (debtors).</note>, this syllable represents the unification back into the Majesty and into the Holy Spirit, as there is no more ill-will. **Gern** <note>The ending of *Schuldigern*.</note>, is the evil child, which now stands before God as God's wonder; from which the will has taken the fault, and desires that the Holy Spirit would receive it into the Majesty as a wonder.

## The Sixth Petition.

36. **Und** <note>And</note>, is once again the casting into the love and gentleness of God, where the soul’s will humbles itself in the Majesty before the Trinity <term>original: "Dreyzahl."</term>. **Füh** <note>The first syllable of *führe* (lead).</note>, there the will travels with the Holy Spirit. **Re** <note>The second syllable of *führe*.</note>, there the will does not wish to travel through the grimness, for it fears the prison of the grimness: for the will shall thus be constantly placed in God, so that it may go through the fire unhurt, and also through the outer Principle <term>original: "Principium." The physical world.</term>, such as this world, and yet should not allow itself to be caught or lusted by anything. But because the soul knows that it did not withstand the first temptation, when it was led into the spirit of this world, as it blew the **Verbum Fiat** <note>Latin: "The Word: Let there be." The creative command used in Genesis, which Böhme links to the formation of the soul's image.</note> into the image; so it now pleads with the Holy Spirit, that He should not enter into the **Proba** <note>Latin: "The trial" or "test."</note> with its will: for it does not trust itself to withstand the devil, if he should sift her; as Christ—

...Christ <note>original: *stus*, the end of *Christus*.</note> spoke to Peter: The Devil has desired to sift you, but I have prayed for you, that your faith may not fail, Luke 22:31. That is, I have enclosed you in the Word, and have not allowed the Devil [access], but through my prayer led you into God's will, so that you were preserved by the Holy Spirit; otherwise you would have been sifted by the Devil through the wrath and spirit of this world. **Uns** <note>The German word for "Us."</note>, this syllable once again encompasses the brotherly unity, as if in one will, into the Majesty, and pleads in the Spirit. **Nicht** <note>The German word for "Not."</note>, in this syllable the will completely tears itself out from the root of wrath, and maintains a special governance outside of the wrath, as the soul then burns out of the fire, and is the true life (outside of the fire) in the light-flaming <term>Tincture</term> <note>In Böhme's alchemy of the soul, the Tincture is the spiritual essence or "dye" that transforms the base quality of wrath into the noble quality of light.</note> in air and power. **In** <note>The first syllable of *In-ver-such-ung* (into temptation).</note>, there it stands as its own sound and being, just as if it were the **Center** <note>original Latin: *Centrum*.</note>. **Ver** <note>The second syllable of *Inversuchung*.</note>, there it must go with the will through the fury <term>original: *Grimm*. This refers to the harsh, fiery wrath of nature or God's "dark side" which must be pacified.</term> and soften it; it must cool it so that it does not ignite it in its gentle life. **Such** <note>The third syllable of *Inversuchung*.</note>, with this syllable it penetrates the fury with its love-tincture, as the **Center of Nature** <note>original Latin: *Centrum Naturæ*. The core point from which natural life and its seven properties arise.</note>, and extinguishes the fury in a Divine manner, and drives the cunning of the Devil out from the fire-source of the original record <note>original: *Urmünde* or *Urkunde*. Böhme often uses terms related to an original testimony or source-spring.</note>, where he would otherwise have access to the soul. **Ung** <note>The final syllable of *Inversuchung*.</note>, there the soul takes with it the power from the 7 forms <note>Böhme's "Seven Qualities" or "Source-Spirits" of nature.</note> of its nature, as a spirit, and sets itself powerfully over the **Center**, and rules over it as a king over his kingdom: for it has now softened and overcome the **Center** with love, and will now let the tempter in no more.

## The Seventh Petition.

37. **Son** <note>The first syllable of *Sondern* (But).</note>, in this syllable it appears in the Majesty with its power and luster over the **Center** of the heart, and has a private **Principle** <note>original Latin: *Principium*. One of the three fundamental realms of Böhme's cosmos: the dark world, the light world, and the outer world.</note> in the Majesty. **Dern** <note>The second syllable of *Sondern*.</note>, there it commands the fury in the **Center**, and rules over it, and tames it with its will. (Just as with Moses, when the fury spoke: Let me be, that I may destroy Israel <note>A reference to Exodus 32:10, where Moses intercedes to stay God's wrath.</note>.) **Er** <note>The first syllable of *Erlöse* (Deliver/Redeem).</note>, there it brings forth a flower and growth out of the **Center**, and opens God’s wonders: for here it deals with the **Center** however it wishes, for it has overcome. **Lö**, this is the growth that grows out of the fury of nature; it is now lovely and good, and is fit for the Kingdom of God. **Se**, there it gran-

## Chapter 16. Of Humanity.

42. O great Depth, why are you so hidden from humanity? It is because they love the devil and the proud wrath <note>original: *Grimm*, Böhme’s term for the harsh, fierce, or wrathful quality of the first "principle" or dark nature</note> more than you; therefore they cannot enter into you! O Mercy of **GOD**, recover once more the tree which you have planted! Why should your anger boast that it has borne more fruit on your tree than your love has!

43. Rebuild Jerusalem, the broken city, so that your kingdom may come and your will be done! Who will give thanks to you in hell? <note>A reference to Psalm 6:5: "For in death there is no remembrance of thee: in the grave who shall give thee thanks?"</note> Clothe us with your Spirit for your praise. How long shall hell drip with fatness? Behold, she has her throat open and wants to swallow us all! Come now and build the city of your forecourt, so that we may live near you, so that your wonders may rejoice when your Spirit of Love judges. Do not delay, Lord, for your tree has grown old with mourning! Bring forth the new and green branch, which grows through the devil’s kingdom against his will: the day is breaking; why then should the night of wrath hold back the lily branch? <note>The "lily branch" (*Lilienzweig*) is Böhme’s symbol for the spiritual rebirth of humanity and a future age of peace and divine knowledge.</note> Lord, your tree grows green through the whole world; therefore wake us up, Lord, so that we may eat of its fruit.

Böhme splits the word to show the beginning (A) and the completion (men).</note>. 49. The Our Father <note>original: *Vater unser*. The Lord's Prayer.</note> is God’s Word, and has seven petitions, an entrance, and an Amen: That is, together, the <term>Number Nine</term> <note>original: *Neun-Zahl*. In Böhme's mystical numerology, 9 represents the realm of spirits and angels just below the absolute unity of God.</note>, and the <term>Number Ten</term> <note>original: *Zehen-Zahl*.</note> is God Himself. With the entrance of the Our Father, the soul’s will goes into the Father, and with the seven petitions it takes what is the Father’s, for by this it becomes an angel again; then, in the seven judgments, it receives the <term>Center of Nature</term> <note>original: *Centrum Naturæ*. This refers to the core of spiritual forces that constitute the inner life of any being.</note> in a heavenly, Divine way, and in the *Amen* it gathers all of this together and dwells within it. For this is the soul's body; it is Christ’s flesh, God’s body: It is the ninth number in the <term>Holy Ternary</term> <note>original: *Ternario Sancto*. Böhme uses this to describe the "holy environment" or the manifested kingdom of the Trinity.</note>. Within this, the <term>Tincture</term> <note>original: *Tinctur*. The will is as subtle as God’s Spirit, and God’s Spirit also travels within the soul’s will; it is his chariot, which he loves.

50. Therefore understand: The naked Deity is Spirit, and as thin as a will; but He has become man, and that thin Spirit of God dwells within humanity, so that our souls may thus easily come to God. And when the soul eats of God’s body in this way, it also receives God’s body upon itself and is God’s child: God is the tree in Christ, and our souls in their holy body are his branches and little twigs.

51. Let this be revealed to you, dear Christendom, from the sunrise to the sunset; the time is near when the Bridegroom wishes to fetch his bride home. Be seeing and not blind: Buy yourselves oil, O you foolish virgins! Depart from the harlotry of the spirit and from pride, or you will not taste this supper. He sets a devouring worm in his heart that plagues him and creates a bad conscience that gnaws at him—and he is only a fool for it. Truly, no greater folly can be found under the sun!

For to each person, his portion is allotted by the spirit of this world, if he would only be content. Thus, one person is the other’s devil, tormenting the other, and it is all for a handful of earth or stones, of which the earth has plenty anyway. Is this not a wonder? Does the fierce hellish spirit not accomplish its wonders according to its desire within mankind, as the Book of Revelation <note>A reference to the biblical Apocalypse, specifically the opening of the Seven Seals.</note> testifies, where one seal of wrath after another has been opened, and men have become servants of that wrath? They have gone forth quite willingly with blood and property; they even thought they were doing God a service thereby.

3. The true human in the heavenly image has no time: His time is like a round crown, or a complete rainbow, which has no beginning and no end. For the image, which is the likeness <term>Likeness: Böhme uses "likeness" (*Gleichnis*) to describe how the human soul acts as a mirror or a correspondence to the divine nature.</term> of God, has neither beginning nor number: It has stood from eternity in God’s Wisdom, as a Virgin without childbearing or without a self-will, for God’s will was the will within her; She was perceived in the Holy Spirit with all the wonders (which we have brought to light and to being in this world). But She was without a body, without essence, and without substances <note>original: *Essentien*. These are the active spiritual forces that comprise the "inner" or spiritual body.</note>: the substances became active within her from the eternal Center upon her creation, as if in three mothers, according to the three principles. That was the creation: that God willed to be revealed in all three mothers. And that was death: that the governance of the image did not remain in its proper order, so that the Middle part moved into the Outer, and the Outer into the Middle; This is not the order of eternity, therefore a breaking apart occurred within this; for the Outer has a beginning and a number within the Middle, and therefore it moves toward an end and must break away from the Middle. This was caused by the craving <note>original: *Sucht*. A term for the fallen "lust" or "sickness" of the soul that pursues material things instead of divine order.</note>, in that it placed the Middle (in which there is an eternal life) into the Outer, and let the Outer into the Middle.

4. Thus life consists of three parts: (1) the Inner, which is God’s eternal hiddenness in the fire, from which life originates; and (2) the Middle, which is from eternity as an image or a likeness of God in

Böhme describes reality as having three principles: the dark fire-world, the light world of God, and this visible world.</note></term>, which is also a figure of the Eternal. And the image became so lost in gazing at this figure that it "imagined" <note>original: *geimaginiret*. To Böhme, imagination is a creative act where the soul "images" itself into something, effectively becoming what it focuses on.</note> and took in the outer image, which must now break away again: But because it is tied by its bond to the eternal <term>Center of Nature<note>original: *Centrum Naturæ*. The spiritual source or "hub" from which all life and movement emerge.</note></term>, this breaking happens painfully according to that same bond, for a life is being broken.

5. When the air ceases, the fire must suffocate and go into the <term>Ether<note>original: *Æther*. The subtle, non-material substance that was believed to fill the universe beyond the earth's atmosphere.</note></term>, which is death: For the outer principle and the inner principle break away from each other; the outer has a beginning, and the inner does not, therefore the outer must break. The outer stands only in the <term>Sun’s Tincture<note>original: *Sonnen Tinctur*. A vitalizing, transformative spiritual power associated with the light and heat of the sun.</note></term>, and its governance is the planets and stars, which always drive their governance toward a goal: For every planet has its goal and a place where it stood during the creation; that is its goal and its <term>Age<note>original: *Seculum*. A cycle of time or a specific era.</note></term>: When it comes to this place, everything over which it was a perfect master is broken, for it begins a new age.

6. But yet you should understand this rightly: Not every one has the <term>Tincture<note>original: *Tinctur*. A medicinal or spiritual essence that can "tint" or transform the quality of a being.</note></term> of life; Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars have the "great life"; Saturn cuts off what he catches at his goal; he does not do it actively, but rather he leaves the life, and so it then has no leader and breaks of its own accord. It happens likewise with the others: But its goal must align in the crown of the stars, in whichever sign and point the planet has its goal; therefore many a young child is already old enough for death while in the mother’s womb, for its master is at the goal and leaves his children. And this is why we cannot fathom our end, because we do not properly know the goal of our leader <note>The "leader" here refers to the governing planet or star under which a person was born.</note>, for we would need to know his number and also the number of the [zodiac] sign if we wished to hit upon our goal.

8. A dead person has no breath, and also has no fire in his body: the body has no sensation, for it breaks apart entirely; its <term>Essences<note>original: *Essentien*. Nothing remains of the outer man; he is gone, for he had a beginning and an end, and all his substance is vanished. Now understand us in this way: just as the Image has stood from eternity in a form—and yet it did not look like any form, but rather like a wonder, as if one dreamed of a vision and an image—so it was foreseen in God's Wisdom with all its wonders.

9. [The soul] dreams of how it is in great torment and anguish, and seeks help everywhere but can see none. Thus it finally despairs and gives itself up to the <term>driver<note>original: *Treiber*. A state of peace within the "holy element," distinct from the higher "Majesty" of the full divine light.</note></term>, as if in the element, and not Majesty; for the transfiguration is unequal, according to each one’s holiness and love.

Heaven and earth, with all their being, lie within man; you must only use the right hammer if you wish to strike his hour and wake him from sleep. # Chapter 18. Of Man.

[how can he] stand before **GOD**, who sits in Christ's chair—which is the place of the **Holy Spirit**—with the heart of a donkey, solely for the sake of wealth and honor? 16. Therefore, let everyone take heed of the <term>vocation<note>original: *Stand*. This refers to one's social standing, class, or profession, which Böhme views as a divine assignment.</note></term> in which they sit. And wherever he is, and whatever he does, he says: "It is my calling, Lord, your will be done; give me what is good for me." Such a person walks rightly in **God’s** wondrous works.

17. But he who is chosen by nature to be a ruler and a leader, especially in the spiritual estate, he had better take good heed of his affairs so that he does not go without weapons. If he remains awake and recognizes that he has **Christ’s** sheep under his pasture, and grazes them rightly as a faithful shepherd, then the shepherd’s staff shall be a great glory to him in eternity. But if he only seeks the wool—his own honor, power, pomp, and magnificence—pursuing his own pleasures and wasting the sheep's fodder, neither feeding nor watering them, but snoring like a sluggard in the lusts of the flesh so that one sheep goes here and another there into error and is eaten by the wolf—one who will not enter the sheepfold but climbs around the outside and looks for how he might craftily steal the sheep's fodder and only shear their wool—all these belong to the wolves and do not have **Christ's** shepherd’s

18. How can someone call himself a shepherd of Christ who has not been chosen by Christ’s Spirit to be a shepherd? Can a wolf also appoint a shepherd over the sheep? Are they not both wolves? Or do we say this out of a desire for conflict? Yet it is established in nature that an evil thing cannot make a good thing out of itself, but only another evil thing. How then can one wrathful soldier pacify another wrathful man, when he himself only wants to murder and strike? Or how will you awaken the **Holy Spirit** in a person when only the spirit of this world is in your voice? That will certainly not happen, unless the Spirit were already awakened in the listener beforehand. Such a listener hears the voice of the **Holy Spirit** in all words spoken concerning **God’s** wonders. And if a donkey could speak <note>A reference to the biblical story of Balaam's donkey in Numbers 22, used here to show that God can use any instrument to reach a prepared soul.</note> and spoke of **God’s** Word, the <term>hammer of the awakener<note>original: *Hammer des Aufweckers*. Böhme’s metaphor for the Holy Spirit or the Divine Word striking the "bell" of the soul to rouse it from spiritual sleep.</note></term> would strike in the soul that is in **God**; for "whoever is of God hears God’s word," says Christ. Therefore, you do not hear because you are not of **God**, but of the Devil and of the spirit of this world.

19. In many people, there is no Word or Spirit of **God** to be awakened at all, for the <term>grim matrix<note>original: *grimme Matrix*. In Böhme's cosmology, the "matrix" is the "mother" or "womb" of nature. The "grim" (wrathful) matrix refers to the harsh, dark, and fiery quality of existence that has not been softened by light and love.</note></term> has captured them. This was shown even when Christ spoke; He certainly held the hammer, but His Spirit does not enter into the malicious, hardened soul, but rather into those who would gladly be pious if only they could. And when the hammer thus awakens the soul-spirit so that the soul turns around and casts itself into **God**, then it is able to do so. The "old man" <note>The "old man" refers to the fallen, ego-driven nature of humanity that must be "put off" to live in the Spirit.</note> must not hold the sovereignty, but rather **God’s** Spirit; otherwise, there is no "ability," but only a clinging to wrath. For there are two <term>cravings<note>original: *Suchten*. While this can mean "sicknesses" or "addictions," in Böhme’s context, it refers to a deep, driving spiritual hunger or impulse.</note></term> in the soul: one is the greedy, grim fire-craving which always seeks the earthly essence; and then there is one from the Spirit, which is born out of the fire, in which we understand the true life of the soul in the **image of God**. This is **God’s** craving, and it seeks the Kingdom of Heaven.

20. Now, if the right hammer strikes therein, as the

# Chapter 18. Of Man.

[...Spirit of] **GOD**, then that same longing becomes so strong that it overcomes the fire-source and longing, and softens it, so that it desires the longing of love as the longing of the soul-spirit; then it is well made: such a soul is easily awakened, so that it constrains the outward governance. And especially when the right <term>hammer of the Holy Spirit<note>Böhme frequently uses the image of a "hammer" to describe the Word of God or the Holy Spirit striking the "bell" of the human soul to rouse it from spiritual sleep.</note></term> sounds through the ears into the heart, the soul's <term>tincture<note>original: *Tincur*. In Böhme's alchemy-influenced theology, the "tincture" is the spiritual essence or "coloring" that defines the quality of a soul or substance.</note></term> quickly catches fire; there it spreads through the entire soul-spirit, through both longings <note>original: *Suchten*. In this context, it refers to the dual driving forces or "passions" within the soul—the dark, fiery desire and the light, loving desire.</note>, for it casts itself into one will. For two wills do not exist in eternity; there must be only One. The one must be as if powerless, and the other almighty; otherwise, there is discord.

21. For this is the law of eternity and eternal existence: that it has only One will. If it had two, one would break the other, and there would be strife. It stands indeed in much power and wonder, but its life is purely and solely love, from which light and majesty proceed. All creatures in heaven have One will, and that is directed into the heart of **GOD**, and goes into **GOD’S** Spirit, certainly in the <term>Center of Multiplicity<note>original: *Centro der Vielheit*. The point of origin from which the diverse variety of created life springs forth.</note></term>, in growth and blossoming. But **GOD’S** Spirit is the life in all things: the <term>Center of Nature<note>original: *Centrum Naturæ*. The core of natural forces and the starting point of the divine manifestation in the physical and spiritual world.</note></term> gives essence, majesty, and power, and the **Holy Spirit** is the leader; He has the supreme governance. Indeed, it has been so from eternity, but in the invisible essence, before the creatures existed.

22. There is nothing new in heaven that has not already been, except that the essence has become tangible: **GOD** has revealed Himself out of Himself in likenesses and images; otherwise, everything is solely **GOD**. The Devil also belongs to **GOD**; he is His wrath in the inner center, which is also the outermost, for his kingdom is the darkness in nature, as mentioned before. Therefore, a man should take care and give birth to himself; for he is a root in **GOD’S** field and has received the spirit for understanding. He should bear a fruit from the soul-spirit in the power of the **Holy Spirit**, not according to the dark form of his "earth" <note>Referring to the fallen, material, or "earthly" aspect of human nature.</note>, but out of the power of the light. For whatever grows out of the power of the light belongs on **GOD’S** table; and what [grows] from the...

<meta>This page concludes Chapter 18 of "The Threefold Life," following the discussion on the necessity of the soul aligning its will with the single, divine will of God to avoid internal discord and strife.</meta>

# III. Of the Threefold Life Chapter 18.

If darkness grows, so that a fruit remains in the darkness, that fruit belongs to the darkness, to the abyss, and to the <term>fierce matrix<note>original: *grimme Matrix*. In Böhme’s cosmology, the "matrix" is the "womb" or generative source of nature. The "fierce" or "wrathful" matrix refers to the harsh, dark quality of the first principle of nature before it is transformed by divine light.</note></term>. After this time, there is no recall or reversal. For as a plant has grown, so it stands and so it tastes; and hereafter it is desired as food only by one who is of the same essences. But whoever does not have these essences does not desire it for food, nor does he gather it.

23. Therefore, let every soul consider and examine itself to see what kind of fruit it is. Here in this life, it is still possible to turn around; one can cut down the herb and bring forth a better plant from the root. But when the <term>great Harvester<note>A reference to the biblical imagery of the Final Judgment, particularly the Parable of the Tares (Matthew 13), where the "reapers" separate the good grain from the weeds.</note></term> comes, he cuts everything down together; then the weeds are bound into bundles and thrown into the fire, but the good herbs are carried to **GOD’S** table.

24. We have revealed this quite faithfully according to our gifts: let whoever hungers eat, and whoever thirsts drink; it is to be taken without money, so that our joy in **GOD** may be complete, and we may also have food to eat in that life. <note>original: *Halleluja, Amen.*</note> Praise the Lord, So be it.
